title: Forward Global announces Venezuela task force
body_text:
EYES ON VENEZUELA : Global public affairs and risk advisory firm Forward Global has launched a new advisory group dedicated to helping clients navigate the rapidly changing political and commercial climate in Venezuela, the firm announced today.

— The Venezuela task force brings together firm experts in the fields of international trade, sanctions compliance, government relations and geopolitical intelligence to advise clients with interests in the South American country that was rocked earlier this month when the United States captured longtime President Nicolás Maduro and his wife and transported the pair to New York City to face drug trafficking charges.

— “Venezuela is entering a transformative phase that will have significant implications for regional stability, energy markets, and cross-border commerce,” Forward Global partner Sven Stumbauer said in a statement. “Organizations need sophisticated analysis and strategic counsel to understand the rapidly evolving landscape and position themselves appropriately.”

— Stumbauer will serve as a member of the Venezuela task force leadership which also includes Jose Mallea , Noe Garcia III , Nicholas Fitzgerald , Judith Jacob , Jonathan Bucks and Juan Nino .

— President Donald Trump has said his administration will indefinitely “run” Venezuela, which had been led by Maduro for more than a decade after the 2013 death of the country’s charismatic socialist leader Hugo Chávez . The administration has sought to work with interim President Delcy Rodríguez on the country’s future, but doubts persist about the level of her cooperation with Washington.

— While the energy industry has a natural interest in the historically oil-rich country , a reset in U.S.-Venezuela relations has the potential to open new commercial opportunities for companies with a strong Washington presence. During a Cabinet meeting today, Trump announced the opening of commercial airspace over Venezuela. American Airlines announced that it will soon resume direct flights to the country, the first U.S. airline to do so since they were prohibited by a 2019 order from the first Trump administration.

title: Kazakhstan hires Continental

FARA FRIDAY: Continental Strategy , the firm founded by former Donald Trump campaign adviser Carlos Trujillo , has been hired to represent the government of Kazakhstan, according to FARA registrations filed with the Justice Department last week.

— The contract, valued at $3.3 million for a year of representation, was signed earlier this month and calls for Continental to provide “government relations services … by facilitating meetings and discussions and establish relationships with key stakeholders in the executive and legislative branches.”

— Trujillo and partner Doug MacGillivray will work on the account, according to separate FARA filings.

— In a statement provided to PI, a firm spokesperson said the contract “reflects the continued growth of our international practice and the trust that both commercial and sovereign clients place in our ability to navigate Washington.”

— “President Trump’s leadership on critical minerals, commercial diplomacy, and supply chain security has created extraordinary opportunities for partnership between the United States and resource-rich allies like Kazakhstan,” the statement added.

— Trujillo and MacGillivray will be joined on the account by Manuel Ortiz of Vantage Knight , a prominent Democratic lobbyist whom Continental has hired as an independent contractor to assist with the Kazakhstan representation. Continental will pay Vantage Knight $1.2 million over the course of this year for Ortiz’s work.

— Kazakhstan has pursued closer ties to the United States in recent months. Kazakh President Kassym - Jomart Tokayev , along with other central Asian leaders, visited the White House in November and announced his nation would be the newest signatory to the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between Israel and several Arab countries. Kazakhstan and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding on critical minerals cooperation during the same visit. And last week, Kazakhstan was announced as one of the founding members of Trump’s Board of Peace.

— On Wednesday, Kazakh energy minister Yerlan Akkenzhenov said the country has submitted a request to the Treasury Department to be allowed to purchase sanctioned Russian oil assets in Kazakhstan.

Happy Friday and welcome to PI . Stay warm this weekend and send tips to dbarnes@politico.com and coprysko@politico.com or send them on Signal at danielbarnes.13 and caitlinoprysko.17 . And don’t forget to follow us on X at @dnlbrns and @caitlinoprysko .

LEHMAN TO PARAMOUNT: Paramount Skydance has tapped Ted Lehman to lead its D.C. office amid the entertainment giant’s hostile takeover bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery , according to a memo sent to staff this morning.

— Lehman was most recently a principal at Todd Strategy Group , where his lobbying clients included Fox Corp. and the cable trade group NCTA , along with health care heavyweights like Eli Lilly , Novo Nordisk , Bayer , AstraZeneca , Amgen , PhRMA , Johnson & Johnson and the American Medical Association .

— In his memo, Paramount chief legal officer Makan Delrahim — who previously led DOJ’s antitrust division during the first Trump administration — said Lehman had been serving as a strategic adviser to the company for the “past few months.”

— Lehman headed downtown in 2022 after more than two decades on the Hill, including serving as chief of staff to Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) and working as a top aide for Republicans on the Senate Judiciary Committee.

— Lehman’s arrival follows the early retirement of the company’s top global lobbyist DeDe Lea . In addition to Paramount’s WBD acquisition push, the company has faced scrutiny from congressional Democrats over CEO David Ellison ’s ties to President Donald Trump and last year’s merger with Skydance. That scrutiny is almost certain to ramp up further after the recent deal to sell TikTok ’s U.S. operations to a group of investors that includes Larry Ellison ’s Oracle .

MORE VENEZUELA: Tower Strategy , the young firm led by retired CIA operations officer Rick de la Torre , is touting its Venezuela bonafides as lobbyists jostle for new business created by the recent U.S. intervention in the South American country.

— This month, the firm hired as a partner Art Estopiñán , who served as chief of staff to then-Rep. Ileana Ros - Lehtinen (R-Fla.) during her time as House Foreign Affairs Committee chair. It also announced Rudolph Atallah , former NSC deputy senior director for counterterrorism; Felipe Garcia Echeverri , former Colombian diplomat; and Tom Naum , president of energy industry supplier REASOL , as strategic partners.

— “Venezuela is not a market you learn from a briefing book,” de la Torre said in a statement. “Our team has dealt with Venezuela as a real-world problem for years, on the ground and inside government. We have worked the policy, security, and energy dimensions under pressure. That experience cannot be improvised, and it matters as the country enters a period of transition.”

PALANTIR MONEY: Amid outrage over the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in Minnesota, a new website aims to reveal the politicians who accept campaign contributions from Palantir , the defense tech company that develops internal systems for ICE, Alex Nguyen reports for Mother Jones .

— “The top six Palantir -funded politicians—via the company’s corporate PAC or individual contributors employed there—are Donald Trump , Sens. John Cornyn (R-Texas) and Bill Cassidy (R-La.), Rep. Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine), and Rep. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.),” he reports.

— Palantir has been granted substantial government contracts during the second Trump administration, and now earns “roughly half of its revenue” from government sales.

MINNESOTA ARRESTS : A lobbyist for the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office was among the people arrested earlier today on charges related to an anti-ICE protest in a Minnesota church last week.

— Jamael Lundy was among the group, which includes former CNN anchor Don Lemon , charged with conspiracy and interfering with a religious service. Lundy is an employee of the county attorney’s office who serves as the prosecutor’s lobbyist to the Minnesota state legislature. He is also a current candidate for the state senate.

— In a statement to local station KARE , the county attorney’s office said Lundy only performs lobbying work and “has no role in the HCAO’s work related to any state investigation.”

— Jim O’Connell will join the American Made Media Company as executive vice president. He is a Trump White House and campaign alum.

— Joey Mott has joined Aflac as federal relations manager. He most recently served as chief of staff to Rep. Ralph Norman (R-S.C.).

— Tim Gibbons has joined the National Family Farm Coalition as its new executive director. He previously served as the communications director for the Missouri Rural Crisis Center .

— Sarah Gerdes has joined Akin as a senior counsel in the firm’s international trade practice. She most recently served as deputy chief of the national security division in the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California.

— Hans Leonard has joined BGR as a director in the firm’s energy and climate group. He most recently worked in the Office of Administrative Litigation at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission.

— Austin Higginbotham will join the Aqui Group , focusing on national security. He currently serves as chief of staff for Rep. Pat Fallon (R-Texas).

— The contract, valued at $3.3 million for a year of representation, was signed earlier this month and calls for Continental to provide “government relations services … by facilitating meetings and discussions and establish relationships with key stakeholders in the executive and legislative branches.”

— Trujillo and partner Doug MacGillivray will work on the account, according to separate FARA filings.

— In a statement provided to PI, a firm spokesperson said the contract “reflects the continued growth of our international practice and the trust that both commercial and sovereign clients place in our ability to navigate Washington.”

— “President Trump’s leadership on critical minerals, commercial diplomacy, and supply chain security has created extraordinary opportunities for partnership between the United States and resource-rich allies like Kazakhstan,” the statement added.

— Trujillo and MacGillivray will be joined on the account by Manuel Ortiz of Vantage Knight, a prominent Democratic lobbyist whom Continental has hired as an independent contractor to assist with the Kazakhstan representation. Continental will pay Vantage Knight $1.2 million over the course of this year for Ortiz’s work.

Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, along with other central Asian leaders, visited the White House in November and announced his nation would be the newest signatory to the Abraham Accords, which normalized relations between Israel and several Arab countries. Kazakhstan and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding on critical minerals cooperation during the same visit. And last week, Kazakhstan was announced as one of the founding members of Trump’s Board of Peace.

title: Travel industry presses to avoid another shutdown travel mess
body_text:
THIS FEELS FAMILIAR: As the House returns to town to squeeze through remaining full-year funding bills and a DHS stopgap, the travel industry — still reeling from last year’s record-breaking shutdown — is pleading with lawmakers to keep the current, partial shutdown as short as possible.

— “When air traffic controllers and TSA officers are forced to work without pay, it strains an already under resourced aviation system and sends ripple effects across the entire travel ecosystem,” the U.S. Travel Association , Airlines for America and the American Hotel & Lodging Association said in a joint statement this morning.

— The groups called on the House to act “with urgency” and pointed out that last fall’s shutdown cost the economy an estimated $6 billion and impacted more than 6 million travelers. “It’s up to the House to pass these measures to prevent significant disruptions, protect travelers, and maintain confidence in the U.S. air travel system,” they said.

— Amid Democratic opposition and efforts from some House Republicans to attach an election citizenship measure to the funding package, an end to the partial shutdown that began over the weekend isn’t likely until tomorrow at the earliest. (President Donald Trump even weighed in on Truth Social this afternoon to urge Democrats and Republicans to support a clean funding package.)

— “Our focus has just been not to try to triage those things or negotiate with unrelated policies, but just to keep focused on the main message,” said Erik Hansen , senior vice president of government relations at U.S. Travel. There are encouraging signs that “Congress has learned the lessons of the damage that it can cause and the havoc that it can create for the economy, but we’re not out of the woods yet,” he told PI.

— The industry has also continued to push for legislation to ensure that FAA employees like air traffic controllers don’t have their pay disrupted by future shutdowns. But though Hansen said there’s been an uptick in interest, others on the Hill haven’t been willing to give up what has become an immense form of leverage in shutdown talks.

— And though we haven’t yet seen the kind of widespread travel disruptions that took place during the last shutdown, Hansen argued that the specter of future shutdowns alone can be a deterrent for hiring crucial aviation workers. “We’re up against a political calculation here, and I don’t think the travel industry should be used as political leverage,” he said.

Kennedy Jr. ’s skeptical views about vaccines. … Now, as Cassidy seeks a third term, Kennedy’s followers haven’t forgiven the senator for grilling Kennedy at that hearing or for criticizing his efforts as health secretary to cast doubt on vaccine safety,” POLITICO ’s Alice Miranda Ollstein and Simon J. title: DC golf course operator lobbies up
body_text:
— National Links Trust , whose 50-year lease to manage the Rock Creek Park, East Potomac and Langston courses was terminated by the administration in December, enlisted Forbes Tate Partners last month to lobby on issues related to “congressional appropriations and public lands management, including operational matters of National Links Trust,” according to a newly filed disclosure. Jeff Strunk , a former top aide to then-House Speaker John Boehner and one of several lobbyists who sits on NTL’s board, will work on the account along with Katie Elliott .

— The nonprofit has pushed back forcefully against the Interior Department’s accusations that it was in default under the lease and amid concerns that the federal takeover will jeopardize affordable access to D.C.’s courses. “We remain stubbornly hopeful that a path forward can be found that preserves affordable and accessible public golf in the nation’s capital for generations to come,” NTL said in a statement following the termination.

MINNESOTA CHAMBER TAPS MICHAEL BEST: The Minnesota Chamber of Commerce has retained Michael Best Strategies , the firm led by former White House chief of staff Reince Priebus , to help the state’s business community navigate the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement surge in Minneapolis.

— Bill McCoshen , a Wisconsin-based lobbyist at the firm, and Alex Angelson , who worked in the West Wing during the first Trump administration, began working for the Minnesota Chamber on Jan. 16, according to a disclosure filing — a week after an ICE agent shot and killed Renee Good and days before immigration agents fatally shot Alex Pretti in Minneapolis.

— Michael Best has been providing the Chamber, whose members include Minnesota-based Cargill , Best Buy , UnitedHealth Group and the Mayo Clinic in addition to companies like Amazon , Delta and Google , with general advice and messaging help as business leaders grapple with how to respond to the heavy-handed federal crackdown and the rifts between federal and local leaders. Chamber spokesperson Matt Bohm told PI that the firm is providing “strategic direction about federal issues relating to Minnesota’s business sector and economy.”

— The Minnesota Chamber posted an open letter last month from more than five dozen business leaders in the state calling for an “immediate deescalation of tensions.” Though the letter steered clear of taking a stance on the immigration crackdown or those protesting it, the missive still marked some of the first public pushback from corporate America.

Happy Wednesday and welcome to PI. Send K Street tips and gossip. You can reach Caitlin on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17 or at coprysko@politico.com . Daniel B. is on Signal at danielbarnes.13 and email at dbarnes@politico.com . Also follow us on X: @caitlinoprysko and @dnlbrns .

MORE NEW BUSINESS: North Carolina has also enlisted Forbes Tate’s help in expediting the flow of federal disaster aid for rebuilding after Hurricane Helene devastated the state in 2024. Holdups of federal assistance and reimbursements have drawn rebukes from Tar Heel State lawmakers on both sides of the aisle and have taken on a starring role in the upcoming Senate race.

— Though DHS announced the release of more than $100 million in Helene recovery aid in January, retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis cited the delays last week in his call for the removal of DHS Secretary Kristi Noem . Last fall, fellow Republican Sen. Ted Budd placed a monthslong hold on several DHS nominees in protest of the bottleneck, while House Democrats from the state introduced legislation in December aimed at circumventing Noem’s directive that she personally approve any DHS expenditures of $100,000 or more.

CORNYN’S CALVALRY: “Some of the country’s richest conservative donors have been pouring tens of millions of dollars into an effort to save Senator John Cornyn of Texas as he faces a daunting Republican primary challenge next month,” The New York Times’ Teddy Schleifer and J. David Goodman report.

— Cornyn’s boosters, which include Blackstone chief executive Stephen Schwarzman and real estate tycoon Harlan Crow , have “spent about $50 million on advertising on his behalf since last July, an unheard-of sum to support a fourth-term incumbent running for re-election in a primary contest.”

— “By contrast, his top challenger, the hard-line Texas attorney general Ken Paxton , has been so confident in his support from the Republican base that he has done barely any advertising at all. The main super PAC supporting Mr. Paxton has so far spent less than 1 percent of the amount spent by Mr. Cornyn’s groups combined.”

— On the Democratic side of the race, top contenders James Talarico and Rep. Jasmine Crockett are rallying donors as they stand up super PACs of their own. A super PAC backing Talarico has already raised $400,000 and is set to go up on the air this week, while Crockett is slated to hit several fundraisers in the San Francisco area next week.

WITH FRIENDS OF THE POD LIKE THESE: “With its interviews of Trump officials, celebrities, and health influencers, [former White House adviser Katie ] Miller launched her eponymous podcast last year, she said, to offer a platform for conservative and MAHA-inclined women. But in a Trump-driven Washington and changing media ecosystem, it’s also offered a prime venue for corporate and special interests looking to shape policy debates,” The Boston Globe ’s Tal Kopan reports.

— “It also raises questions about what ethical guardrails exist between the show, Katie Miller’s private business interests, and the administration, where she and her husband, the White House deputy chief of staff, have deep professional and social connections. Though ethics experts said there’s nothing novel about a D.C. power couple where one works in government and the other represents outside interests, it can appear unseemly to the public even if it doesn’t run afoul of explicit rules.”

D.C. GOLF COURSES HIRE FORBES TATE: The nonprofit that oversees Washington’s three public golf courses has lobbied up as it prepares to fight President Donald Trump’s move to take over the courses.

— National Links Trust, whose 50-year lease to manage the Rock Creek Park, East Potomac and Langston courses was terminated by the administration in December, enlisted Forbes Tate Partners last month to lobby on issues related to “congressional appropriations and public lands management, including operational matters of National Links Trust,” according to a newly filed disclosure. Jeff Strunk, a former top aide to then-House Speaker John Boehner and one of several lobbyists who sits on NTL’s board, will work on the account along with Katie Elliott.

— The nonprofit has pushed back forcefully against the Interior Department’s accusations that it was in default under the lease and amid concerns that the federal takeover will jeopardize affordable access to D.C.’s courses. “We remain stubbornly hopeful that a path forward can be found that preserves affordable and accessible public golf in the nation’s capital for generations to come,” NTL said in a statement following the termination.

MINNESOTA CHAMBER TAPS MICHAEL BEST: The Minnesota Chamber of Commerce has retained Michael Best Strategies, the firm led by former White House chief of staff Reince Priebus, to help the state’s business community navigate the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement surge in Minneapolis.

— Bill McCoshen, a Wisconsin-based lobbyist at the firm, and Alex Angelson, who worked in the West Wing during the first Trump administration, began working for the Minnesota Chamber on Jan. 16, according to a disclosure filing — a week after an ICE agent shot and killed Renee Good and days before immigration agents fatally shot Alex Pretti in Minneapolis.

— Michael Best has been providing the Chamber, whose members include Minnesota-based Cargill, Best Buy, UnitedHealth Group and the Mayo Clinic in addition to companies like Amazon, Delta and Google, with general advice and messaging help as business leaders grapple with how to respond to the heavy-handed federal crackdown and the rifts between federal and local leaders. Chamber spokesperson Matt Bohm told PI that the firm is providing “strategic direction about federal issues relating to Minnesota’s business sector and economy.”

— The Minnesota Chamber posted an open letter last month from more than five dozen business leaders in the state calling for an “immediate deescalation of tensions.” Though the letter steered clear of taking a stance on the immigration crackdown or those protesting it, the missive still marked some of the first public pushback from corporate America.

The main super PAC supporting Mr. Paxton has so far spent less than 1 percent of the amount spent by Mr. Cornyn’s groups combined.”

title: Iceland lobbies up after ‘52nd state’ crack
body_text:
FARA FRIDAY: The Icelandic government has hired Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck to represent the island in Washington, less than a month after a quip from President Donald Trump ’s pick for ambassador about annexing the country sparked a brief diplomatic frenzy.

— Iceland retained Brownstein beginning this week to provide “strategic advice on navigating engagements” with U.S. officials, according to documents filed with the Justice Department. The six-month contract comes with a monthly retainer of $25,000.

— Their work will include helping Iceland make inroads with the federal government by brokering introductions and meetings with key stakeholders, developing strategies and tactics for its engagement with Washington. Brownstein will also serve as “a consultive [sic] resource and provide constructive feedback on emerging priorities for the Government of Iceland,” filings show.

— Former diplomat Samantha Carl-Yoder will work on the account for Brownstein along with Brandt Anderson , a former national security adviser to Sen. Todd Young (R-Ind.); Brady Howell , an alum of the first Trump administration and former staffer on the House Foreign Affairs Committee; Tom Wotka , a former State Department energy official; and Jason Buckner , a former top lobbyist for the mining company BHP .

— Tensions between the U.S. and Iceland flared last month when Billy Long , the former Missouri representative and IRS chief and Trump’s nominee as ambassador to Iceland, joked to former colleagues on the House floor that the NATO ally would become the 52nd U.S. state — and Long, its governor.

— The comment, which Long apologized for a day later , set off a panic in Reykjavík, particularly given Trump’s escalating rhetoric at the time about taking over Greenland (by force if necessary). Icelanders started a petition demanding that the government reject Long as envoy.

— According to a Jan. 23 cable obtained by POLITICO ’s Nahal Toosi , Paul McLeary and Victor Jack , “Iceland’s Permanent Secretary of State Martin Eyjólfsson summoned U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Erin Sawyer to demand a high-level U.S. apology and tell her that such talk ‘has no place in international discourse.’”

TGIF and welcome to PI. Send K Street tips and gossip. You can reach Caitlin on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17 or at coprysko@politico.com . Daniel B. is on Signal at danielbarnes.13 and email at dbarnes@politico.com . Also follow us on X: @caitlinoprysko and @dnlbrns .

DOJ MOVES TO QUASH WILES SUBPOENA: Federal prosecutors in Miami and Washington last night formally moved to quash an effort by former Rep. David Rivera to compel testimony by White House chief of staff Susie Wiles in Rivera’s trial next month on foreign agent charges.

— Defense attorneys for the former Florida Congress member and his co-defendant, political consultant Esther Nuhfer , moved to subpoena Wiles for her testimony back in December, explaining that they wanted to question Wiles about her “extensive communications” related to her lobbying work at Ballard Partners for a Venezuelan businessman who prosecutors say was involved in Rivera’s work as an unregistered agent of the Venezuelan government. Rivera and Nuhfer are also seeking testimony from Secretary of State Marco Rubio .

— But in a filing last night , the lead prosecutors on the case as well as an attorney from DOJ’s National Security Division in Washington sought to have the subpoena thrown out “due to the fact that, based on the government’s investigation in this matter, Ms. Wiles appears to have played no role in any of the relevant events.”

— At the very least, prosecutors asked District Court Judge Melissa Damian to put Wiles’ subpoena on hold “pending a more extensive factual record to be developed at trial … to better assess the potential relevance (or lack thereof) of her testimony based on the actual defense the defendants pursue at trial.”

— Prosecutors argued that Wiles’ lack of involvement is illustrated by the fact that investigators never even interviewed her. Ballard’s work for the Venezuelan TV network Globovision was not central to the core allegations of the case, they added, questioning how additional context about the firm’s work might exculpate Rivera and Nuhfer in the case.

AIPAC WHIFFS: “The American Israel Public Affairs Committee uncorked $2 million to try to sink a mainstream Democrat in a multi-candidate special House election primary in New Jersey — and it’s infuriating mainstream Democrats and some of the pro-Israel lobby’s supporters,” POLITICO ’s Elena Schneider writes.

— “The organization spent heavily through its super PAC, Unite Democracy Project , to attack former Rep. Tom Malinowski (D-N.J.), a pro-Israel moderate who would not support unconditional aid to Israel. In doing so, it provided an opening to Analilia Mejia , a progressive organizer backed by Bernie Sanders who has said Israel committed genocide in Gaza” and who’s leading Malinowski by roughly 500 votes to fill the seat vacated by new Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill .

— “The first test of the group’s muscle ahead of the 2026 primary season, when they are expected to spend millions on Democratic primaries across the country,” AIPAC’s “first foray of 2026 backfired spectacularly.”

COUPANG’S COUP: “A closed-door congressional meeting this week with South Korea’s top trade official was dominated by one topic: Coupang Inc. , the Seattle-headquartered e-commerce platform best known as the ‘ Amazon of South Korea,’” which is facing an intense probe in the country over a massive data breach there last year, per Bloomberg ’s Emily Birnbaum.

— The grilling “comes amid an intense lobbying push by Coupang, which employs just 1,000 people in the US but has ties that go as high as Kevin Warsh ,” Trump’s Fed chair nominee. The company has poured at least $5.5 million into its lobbying blitz over the last two years, winning defenders as ideologically diverse as Vice President JD Vance and Virginia Democratic Rep. Don Beyer .

— “The e-commerce platform has also opened a new Pennsylvania Avenue office just blocks from the White House and the US Capitol and partnered with Washington’s beloved Capitals hockey team. Warsh has been a Coupang board member since 2019 and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has ties to early Coupang investor Stanley Druckenmiller ” — a remarkably “high visibility for a company that is little known to most US consumers.”

BALLARD’S FOREIGN CASH BONANZA: Ballard Partners “has drawn a surge of high-paying clients with foreign interests seeking access to the administration and federal agencies,” Sludge ’s David Moore reports.

— “Many of its biggest spenders in 2025 were foreign companies or clients with significant foreign business interests. Ballard reported millions of dollars in payments from clients including oil and gas company Balkan Energy , based in Albania; TotalEnergies , for its liquified natural gas project in Mozambique; critical minerals company Korea Zinc ; and TikTok , as its Chinese owner ByteDance negotiated new U.S. ownership.”

— “Several more of Ballard’s top lobbying clients have foreign ties: one is the New Era Fund … a defense and aerospace investment fund for ventures with Saudi Arabia. A second is the holding company of Bancrédito , a Puerto Rican bank in liquidation after a bribery scandal. A third is the former fugitive and cryptocurrency billionaire Roger Ver , who cut a deal with the Department of Justice (DOJ) over tax evasion charges after living in Mallorca.”

— “Nearly all of these clients hired Ballard Partners after Trump’s election win—quickly becoming among the firm’s top lobbying spenders. … And nearly all have benefited directly from Trump administration actions. Altogether, these seven clients paid the firm more than $7 million for lobbying during Trump’s first year back in office, and three of them were its top spenders.”

Iceland lobbies up after ‘52nd state’ crack

By CAITLIN OPRYSKO 

02/06/2026 06:42 PM EST

Presented by

With Daniel Lippman

FARA FRIDAY: The Icelandic government has hired Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck to represent the island in Washington, less than a month after a quip from President Donald Trump’s pick for ambassador about annexing the country sparked a brief diplomatic frenzy.

— Iceland retained Brownstein beginning this week to provide “strategic advice on navigating engagements” with U.S. officials, according to documents filed with the Justice Department. The six-month contract comes with a monthly retainer of $25,000.

— Their work will include helping Iceland make inroads with the federal government by brokering introductions and meetings with key stakeholders, developing strategies and tactics for its engagement with Washington. Brownstein will also serve as “a consultive [sic] resource and provide constructive feedback on emerging priorities for the Government of Iceland,” filings show.

— Former diplomat Samantha Carl-Yoder will work on the account for Brownstein along with Brandt Anderson, a former national security adviser to Sen. Todd Young (R-Ind.); Brady Howell, an alum of the first Trump administration and former staffer on the House Foreign Affairs Committee; Tom Wotka, a former State Department energy official; and Jason Buckner, a former top lobbyist for the mining company BHP.

— Tensions between the U.S. and Iceland flared last month when Billy Long, the former Missouri representative and IRS chief and Trump’s nominee as ambassador to Iceland, joked to former colleagues on the House floor that the NATO ally would become the 52nd U.S. state — and Long, its governor.

— The comment, which Long apologized for a day later, set off a panic in Reykjavík, particularly given Trump’s escalating rhetoric at the time about taking over Greenland (by force if necessary). Icelanders started a petition demanding that the government reject Long as envoy.

— According to a Jan. 23 cable obtained by POLITICO’s Nahal Toosi, Paul McLeary and Victor Jack, “Iceland’s Permanent Secretary of State Martin Eyjólfsson summoned U.S. Chargé d’Affaires Erin Sawyer to demand a high-level U.S. apology and tell her that such talk ‘has no place in international discourse.’”

TGIF and welcome to PI. Send K Street tips and gossip. You can reach Caitlin on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17 or at coprysko@politico.com. Daniel B. is on Signal at danielbarnes.13 and email at dbarnes@politico.com. Also follow us on X: @caitlinoprysko and @dnlbrns.

DOJ MOVES TO QUASH WILES SUBPOENA: Federal prosecutors in Miami and Washington last night formally moved to quash an effort by former Rep. David Rivera to compel testimony by White House chief of staff Susie Wiles in Rivera’s trial next month on foreign agent charges.

— Defense attorneys for the former Florida Congress member and his co-defendant, political consultant Esther Nuhfer, moved to subpoena Wiles for her testimony back in December, explaining that they wanted to question Wiles about her “extensive communications” related to her lobbying work at Ballard Partners for a Venezuelan businessman who prosecutors say was involved in Rivera’s work as an unregistered agent of the Venezuelan government. Rivera and Nuhfer are also seeking testimony from Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

— But in a filing last night, the lead prosecutors on the case as well as an attorney from DOJ’s National Security Division in Washington sought to have the subpoena thrown out “due to the fact that, based on the government’s investigation in this matter, Ms. Wiles appears to have played no role in any of the relevant events.”

— At the very least, prosecutors asked District Court Judge Melissa Damian to put Wiles’ subpoena on hold “pending a more extensive factual record to be developed at trial … to better assess the potential relevance (or lack thereof) of her testimony based on the actual defense the defendants pursue at trial.”

— Prosecutors argued that Wiles’ lack of involvement is illustrated by the fact that investigators never even interviewed her. Ballard’s work for the Venezuelan TV network Globovision was not central to the core allegations of the case, they added, questioning how additional context about the firm’s work might exculpate Rivera and Nuhfer in the case.

AIPAC WHIFFS: “The American Israel Public Affairs Committee uncorked $2 million to try to sink a mainstream Democrat in a multi-candidate special House election primary in New Jersey — and it’s infuriating mainstream Democrats and some of the pro-Israel lobby’s supporters,” POLITICO’s Elena Schneider writes.

— “The organization spent heavily through its super PAC, Unite Democracy Project, to attack former Rep. Tom Malinowski (D-N.J.), a pro-Israel moderate who would not support unconditional aid to Israel. In doing so, it provided an opening to Analilia Mejia, a progressive organizer backed by Bernie Sanders who has said Israel committed genocide in Gaza” and who’s leading Malinowski by roughly 500 votes to fill the seat vacated by new Democratic Gov. Mikie Sherrill.

— “The first test of the group’s muscle ahead of the 2026 primary season, when they are expected to spend millions on Democratic primaries across the country,” AIPAC’s “first foray of 2026 backfired spectacularly.”

COUPANG’S COUP: “A closed-door congressional meeting this week with South Korea’s top trade official was dominated by one topic: Coupang Inc., the Seattle-headquartered e-commerce platform best known as the ‘Amazon of South Korea,’” which is facing an intense probe in the country over a massive data breach there last year, per Bloomberg’s Emily Birnbaum.

— The grilling “comes amid an intense lobbying push by Coupang, which employs just 1,000 people in the US but has ties that go as high as Kevin Warsh,” Trump’s Fed chair nominee. The company has poured at least $5.5 million into its lobbying blitz over the last two years, winning defenders as ideologically diverse as Vice President JD Vance and Virginia Democratic Rep. Don Beyer.

— “The e-commerce platform has also opened a new Pennsylvania Avenue office just blocks from the White House and the US Capitol and partnered with Washington’s beloved Capitals hockey team. Warsh has been a Coupang board member since 2019 and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has ties to early Coupang investor Stanley Druckenmiller” — a remarkably “high visibility for a company that is little known to most US consumers.”

BALLARD’S FOREIGN CASH BONANZA: Ballard Partners “has drawn a surge of high-paying clients with foreign interests seeking access to the administration and federal agencies,” Sludge’s David Moore reports.

— “Many of its biggest spenders in 2025 were foreign companies or clients with significant foreign business interests. Ballard reported millions of dollars in payments from clients including oil and gas company Balkan Energy, based in Albania; TotalEnergies, for its liquified natural gas project in Mozambique; critical minerals company Korea Zinc; and TikTok, as its Chinese owner ByteDance negotiated new U.S. ownership.”

— “Several more of Ballard’s top lobbying clients have foreign ties: one is the New Era Fund … a defense and aerospace investment fund for ventures with Saudi Arabia. A second is the holding company of Bancrédito, a Puerto Rican bank in liquidation after a bribery scandal. A third is the former fugitive and cryptocurrency billionaire Roger Ver, who cut a deal with the Department of Justice (DOJ) over tax evasion charges after living in Mallorca.”

— “Nearly all of these clients hired Ballard Partners after Trump’s election win—quickly becoming among the firm’s top lobbying spenders. … And nearly all have benefited directly from Trump administration actions. Altogether, these seven clients paid the firm more than $7 million for lobbying during Trump’s first year back in office, and three of them were its top spenders.”

title: Netflix hires another antitrust lobbyist
body_text:
NETFLIX HIRES APELBAUM: Netflix added yet another antitrust lobbyist at the start of the year, according to a newly filed disclosure, as details of the streaming giant’s growing army of lobbyists continue to trickle out. Kressin Powers’ Perry Apelbaum , a longtime top Democratic lawyer on the House Judiciary Committee, began lobbying for Netflix last month on antitrust issues in the tech industry.

— After 30 years with the Judiciary Committee, Apelbaum in 2021 joined the Justice Department as a senior counsel in the antitrust division; he also served as deputy assistant attorney general in the legislative affairs office. He joined Kressin Powers (formerly known as Kressin Meador Powers ) last spring following former partner Mark Meador ’s nomination to join the FTC.

— As PI has previously noted , Netflix has been scooping up veteran antitrust lobbyists left and right since announcing its plans to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery and the ensuing torrent of concern from official Washington and the entertainment industry.

S-3 GROUP ADDS DEM FINANCE AIDE: Chris Arneson , one of the top Democratic aides on the powerful Senate Finance Committee, is leaving the Hill after nearly a decade and a half to join S-3 Group as a principal. Arneson was most recently economic policy director for ranking member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), helping oversee outreach to the business community and other stakeholders and managing the committee’s strategic initiatives and policy coordination.

— Over the years, he’s also served as the panel’s chief budget and economic adviser, senior tax policy adviser and research assistant over the years — giving Arneson a front row seat to some of the pivotal legislative fights including last year’s GOP reconciliation bill and the party’s 2017 tax overhaul, the 2023 debt ceiling fight and the 2022 Democratic reconciliation package.

— At S-3 Group, Arneson told PI that he expects to work on many of those same issues, especially as tax, trade and health care continue to dominate policy conversations, with an expected Supreme Court ruling on tariffs; a potential second, health care-focused reconciliation bill or tax package on the Hill; and implementation of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act continuing in the executive branch.

— “I have great relationships after 15 years … on the Finance Committee, as well as with our down-dais members” on both sides of the aisle, he said in an interview, “so hoping that I’ll get to keep doing the same issues I’ve been doing, just from a different approach.” Arneson plans on registering to lobby.

— Though S-3 Group is home to several top former aides to House Majority Leader Steve Scalise and saw its annual lobbying revenues surge 63 percent last year under full GOP control of Washington, the firm also employs a number of Democratic lobbyists, including former aides to House Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.), former Senate Approps Chair Pat Leahy (D-Vt.), former Senate HELP Chair Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and the DNC .

Happy Monday and welcome to PI. Send K Street tips and gossip. You can reach Caitlin on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17 or at coprysko@politico.com . Daniel B. is on Signal at danielbarnes.13 and email at dbarnes@politico.com . Also follow us on X: @caitlinoprysko and @dnlbrns .

FLYING IN: Hundreds of nurse practitioners are in town this week as part of a fly-in organized by the American Association of Nurse Practitioners . They’ll hit the Hill tomorrow with a focus on rallying opposition to a rule proposed by the Trump administration that would remove nurse practitioner programs from the definition of “professional degree” for purposes of federal student loan eligibility, which AANP has said the rule would be “disastrous” for the industry.

WHAT PARSCALE IS DOING FOR ISRAEL: “Since November, an unspecified number of Americans have been receiving text messages from unknown numbers claiming to be from organizations called ‘Friends for Peace’ and ‘Partners in Peace’ asking their views on Israel, promoting Israel as a U.S. ally, and pushing links to websites and videos created by Clock Tower X ,” the firm founded by former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale that inked a $9 million contract with the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs last year, according to new details of the campaign unearthed by Responsible Statecraft ’s Nick Cleveland-Stout .

ANNALS OF FUNDRAISING: “President Trump’s allies are offering access to him and other perks to donors who give at least $1 million to a new group supporting flashy initiatives he is planning around the nation’s 250th birthday,” per The New York Times’ Ken Vogel , Lisa Friedman and David A. Fahrenthold .

— “The group, Freedom 250 , is threatening to overshadow years of plans meant to reach the broadest cross section of Americans for semiquincentennial celebrations. They are now taking on a Trumpian flare, replete with marble and machismo.”

— “But Freedom 250 has also emerged as another vehicle, akin to the White House ballroom project , through which people and companies with interests before the Trump administration can make tax-deductible donations to gain access to, and seek favor with, a president who has maintained a keen interest in fund-raising, and a willingness to use the levers of government power to reward financial supporters.”

OURA’S AURA: “ Oura rings are on fingers from the Pentagon to Capitol Hill, tracking everything from sleep quality to fertility. Their Finnish maker’s success stems from design savvy and good timing, but also shrewd attention to the way politics works in the capital,” POLITICO ’s Amanda Chu reports.

— “The company in the last year has hired top lobbying shops with links to the administration and Republican lawmakers in Congress, boosting its lobbying spend from $40,000 in 2024 to more than $1 million a year. … [I]t’s got a message that resonates: The rings are a solution to systemic health care challenges no one has been able to fix, ranging from physician shortages to ballooning federal spending.”

— “It’s paying off. The Defense Department, Oura’s largest customer, now provides rings to certain soldiers and civil servants as an employee benefit. … Besides buying the rings, lawmakers have gone to bat to protect Oura from Chinese and Indian competitors. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has made wearables like the Oura ring part of his Make America Healthy Again movement.”

TAKING STOCK: “At least nine senators reported stock purchases or sales last year involving companies in industries overseen by the committees they serve on,” according to CNN ’s Annie Grayer and Marshall Cohen , a trend worrying watchdogs as an effort to ban the practice loses steam on the Hill.

— “Most of the nine senators who invested in stocks that overlap with their committee assignments over the last year have comprehensive financial portfolios, not all of which raise potential conflict-of-interest issues. … But the more than a dozen trades from this small group of well-connected senators provide a window into why the phenomenon of lawmaker stock-trading has led to public outrage – and a major push to ban the practice.”

NAM KICKS OFF SURFACE TRANSPORTATION PUSH: The National Association of Manufacturers is pumping six figures into a lobbying blitz aimed at getting a surface transportation reauthorization bill and permitting reform across the finish line by the time the current authorization bill lapses Sept. 30.

— NAM’s Building to Win campaign reprises the trade group’s earlier pushes for infrastructure investment beginning a decade ago, culminating in 2021’s bipartisan infrastructure bill and last year’s House passage of permitting reforms. In addition to a nationwide ad campaign, NAM is also circulating a graphic mapping out the nation’s 25 worst freight bottlenecks and how that congestion near transportation hubs can cost the manufacturing industry billions annually.

CHANGING OF THE GUARD: The Consumer Technology Association ’s Gary Shapiro is stepping down as CEO of the trade group after 35 years at the helm. Kinsey Fabrizio , who’s been with CTA group for nearly two decades and became its president in 2024, will add chief executive to that title beginning in May. Shapiro will stay on as executive chair.

— Fabrizio joined CTA in 2008 as a manager of member programs, before working her way up to senior vice president of membership and head of CES — the trade group’s massive annual tech trade show.

— She’ll take the helm of CTA at a crucial time for the tech industry, as tech products and artificial intelligence continue to infiltrate every aspect of life across the globe, even absent a federal regulatory framework for the technology in the U.S.

— Shapiro and CTA have also been among the most vocal opponents of President Donald Trump ’s tariffs, and CTA was one of the only major business groups to lend its voice in support of the Supreme Court case challenging the duties. “There is a time for everything, and I’m pleased with the new opportunities for CTA and for my next chapter,” Shapiro said in a statement, calling the transition long-planned.

— CTA’s members include Amazon , Google , Sony , Samsung , Best Buy , Microsoft , Meta and AMD . And though the association’s lobbying outlays pale in comparison to many of its most prominent members and fellow tech organizations, CTA ranks among the largest trade groups in Washington with nearly $154 million in revenue in 2024, tax filings show. That’s a tenfold expansion from when Shapiro took the helm, according to CTA.

ANOTHER SENATE FINANCE AIDE HEADS DOWNTOWN: Courtney Connell has left the Hill after five years serving as a top tax aide for the Senate Finance Committee to join Washington Council Ernst & Young as a partner/principal. Connell most recently served as chief tax counsel to Finance Chair Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), where she played an instrumental role in crafting last summer’s GOP reconciliation bill.

— Before joining the Finance Committee under then-Chair Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) in 2020, Connell completed stints as a senior director of tax at Anheuser-Busch InBev , a senior tax counsel at MetLife , a manager at EY and tax counsel in the IRS’ Office of Chief Counsel.

— Connell is the latest staffer who worked on the reconciliation bill to head to K Street since its passage last summer. Holland & Knight later added Chris Jaarda , the former senior policy adviser and counsel to House Speaker Mike Johnson .

— Kathryn Reed , a tax adviser to House Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith (R-Mo.) decamped for BGR Group in November, while former Ways and Means general counsel and parliamentarian Molly Fromm joined the Nickles Group in May. A16Z ASCENDANT: Andreessen Horowitz , “one of Silicon Valley’s most storied venture capital firms has emerged as a hidden hand steering artificial intelligence policy in Washington, as President Donald Trump embraces the industry’s relentless push into the emerging technology,” Bloomberg ’s Emily Birnbaum and Oma Seddiq report.

— “Andreessen Horowitz is now regularly the first outside call that top White House officials and senior Republican congressional aides make when considering moves that could affect tech companies’ AI plans, according to current and former White House and congressional aides. FLYING IN: HVAC manufacturers with the Air-Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute are fanning out across the Hill this week to press lawmakers for updates to modernize a landmark energy law, the Energy Policy and Conservation Act.

— The coalition will focus on striking down state laws that impose certain in-person requirements for estate planning such as ink signatures and paper processing, arguing that modernization will expand access to those services and is more secure.

title: K Street mines critical minerals
body_text:
CRITICAL LOBBYING : Ramping up critical minerals production in the U.S. involves a heady cocktail of domestic permitting reform, international infrastructure development and price floors — and that’s where lobbying giant Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck is stepping in.

— Brownstein’s new critical minerals practice, reported first in PI, will be led by co-chairs former foreign service officer Samantha Carl-Yoder and Obama alum Jason Buckner . The firm already has a significant number of critical mineral clients, but the formalization of the practice will enable more specialization for what the industry could need, Carl-Yoder told your host in an interview.

— The Trump administration is eager to dethrone China as top dog in the fight for critical minerals, but it’s easier said than done. Just last week, the administration called on more than 50 countries to join a trading bloc to counter China’s dominance in both mining and processing — but only 11 countries signed on to the nonbinding agreement. That could be partly due to the administration’s aggressive foreign policy positions and punitive tariff regime of the past year, as my colleagues previously reported.

— Navigating President Donald Trump ’s mercurial foreign policy will likely be a key challenge. “A lot of the underlining scope is, how do you improve U.S. resilience? How do you address supply chain issues? How do you make sure you’re working with allied partners?” said Carl-Yoder, who spoke to your host from the Mining Indaba conference in Cape Town, South Africa. “Sometimes that works better than it does other times.”

— Domestically, Buckner told your host he’s already working with clients on permitting reform, capital access and navigating the National Environmental Policy Act process.

— Some of Brownstein’s clients include: Ivanhoe Mines , Ivanhoe Atlantic , Ivanhoe Electric , Boston Metal , Heeney Capital and Albemarle .

Happy Thursday and welcome to PI. I’m your host, Marcia Brown, happy to be here while Caitlin is off. Daniel Lippman will be writing tomorrow. Add me on Signal at marciagbrown.68 or email me at marciabrown@politico.com .

Say hello and send influence tips to Daniel L. at dlippman@politico.com . And be sure to follow us all on X at @AlexGangitano , @Marcia_Brown9 and @dlippman .

Programming note: We’ll be off this Monday but back in your inboxes on Tuesday.

ICYMI — KENNEDY CENTER SAGA : Trump “has brought in his top fundraiser to shore up giving at the Kennedy Center after a series of stumbles by its development leader, a former TV host close to Kari Lake , according to six people familiar with the matter,” our Daniel Lippman scooped last night.

— “Trump intervened in January and tapped his longtime supporter Meredith O’Rourke to stabilize the Kennedy Center’s fundraising operation, in a move that effectively sidelined senior vice president Lisa Dale , according to three current and one former employee.”

— “O’Rourke is also in charge of fundraising for the new White House ballroom and helped raise the money to replace the Rose Garden with a paved patio.”

MIDTERM MONEY : “Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic announced Thursday that it is donating $20 million to Public First Action , a political action committee set up to support candidates who favor AI regulations in the midterm elections,” our Brendon Bordelon reported Thursday.

— “Anthropic’s $20-million infusion into Public First, a 501(c)(4), comes days after an AI industry super PAC, Leading the Future , announced it has so far raised $125 million. Leading the Future aims to support AI-industry friendly candidates, and its donors include venture capitalist firm Andreessen Horowitz , OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale .”

FOREIGN DONATIONS: American colleges and universities have so far reported receiving more than $5.2 billion in foreign gifts and contracts last year, the Trump administration disclosed Wednesday as it presses ahead with investigations into four schools’ foreign ties, our Juan Perez Jr. reports in Morning Education .

The latest available numbers in the Education Department’s new foreign funding reporting portal now reflect approximately $67.6 billion in total foreign funding that institutions have reported receiving since 1986, Juan adds.

THE BLUE ZONE — Washingtonian’s Jessica Sidman reports that Rhonda Foxx , who served as national women’s engagement director for both the Biden and Harris campaigns, has opened Civic, a cafe and bar — a “Butterworth’s for like-minded individuals,” Foxx said, referencing the MAGA locale . (H/t POLITICO Playbook)

— But, but but: D.C. is already a deep-blue city. “‘Why don’t we have a lib Butterworth’s?’ Er... you mean like every other restaurant and coffee shop in DC?” White House deputy press secretary Abigail Jackson said on X .

MARRIAGE BOOTCAMP : The Heritage Foundation is drawing online criticism, per USA Today’s Kate Perez , for a policy proposal to boost birthrates that would involve marriage bootcamps.

— “The online report, titled ‘Saving America by Saving the Family: A Foundation for the Next 250 Years,’ published Jan. 8 by The Heritage Foundation, lays out ways the group says the United States can ‘restore the family home,’ including through monetarily incentivizing couples to have children and stay married, among other efforts,” Perez reports.

— The marriage bootcamps would “cover topics like communication, money management and conflict resolution for ‘cohabiting couples with children.’”

— “The successful completion of the program would conclude with couples ‘ready to walk down the aisle at a communal wedding,’ the report states, and a potential $5,000 monetary incentive − funded by foundations or private donors − for couples to get married. Additionally, newlyweds would leave with a mentor couple to guide them through marriage following the wedding.”

EAT YOUR VEGGIES : The International Fresh Produce Association is delivering produce boxes including apples, oranges, squash, onions and tomatoes to 100 House and Senate offices with the message “You can’t ‘Make America Healthy Again’ without fruits and vegetables!”

FLYING IN : The American Association of Port Authorities will host its fly-in March 4, during the group’s annual legislative summit. Members will meet with congressional offices to urge changes to the Water Resources Development Act and more investments in the Port Infrastructure Development Program among other issues.

AD SPLASH: The Steel Manufacturers Association launched a six-figure ad campaign across broadcast and digital channels — “Steel Strong” — on how the Section 232 steel tariffs are strengthening the domestic steel industry.

SPOTTED at NCTA — The Internet & Television Association’ s Congressional Wi-Fi Caucus event with WifiForward : Sens. Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) and Pete Ricketts (R-Neb.); Reps. CRITICAL LOBBYING: Ramping up critical minerals production in the U.S. involves a heady cocktail of domestic permitting reform, international infrastructure development and price floors — and that’s where lobbying giant Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck is stepping in.

— Brownstein’s new critical minerals practice, reported first in PI, will be led by co-chairs former foreign service officer Samantha Carl-Yoder and Obama alum Jason Buckner. The firm already has a significant number of critical mineral clients, but the formalization of the practice will enable more specialization for what the industry could need, Carl-Yoder told your host in an interview.

— The Trump administration is eager to dethrone China as top dog in the fight for critical minerals, but it’s easier said than done. Just last week, the administration called on more than 50 countries to join a trading bloc to counter China’s dominance in both mining and processing — but only 11 countries signed on to the nonbinding agreement. That could be partly due to the administration’s aggressive foreign policy positions and punitive tariff regime of the past year, as my colleagues previously reported.

— Navigating President Donald Trump’s mercurial foreign policy will likely be a key challenge. “A lot of the underlining scope is, how do you improve U.S. resilience? How do you address supply chain issues? How do you make sure you’re working with allied partners?” said Carl-Yoder, who spoke to your host from the Mining Indaba conference in Cape Town, South Africa. “Sometimes that works better than it does other times.”

— Domestically, Buckner told your host he’s already working with clients on permitting reform, capital access and navigating the National Environmental Policy Act process.

— Some of Brownstein’s clients include: Ivanhoe Mines, Ivanhoe Atlantic, Ivanhoe Electric, Boston Metal, Heeney Capital and Albemarle.

Happy Thursday and welcome to PI. I’m your host, Marcia Brown, happy to be here while Caitlin is off. Daniel Lippman will be writing tomorrow. Add me on Signal at marciagbrown.68 or email me at marciabrown@politico.com.

Say hello and send influence tips to Daniel L. at dlippman@politico.com. And be sure to follow us all on X at @AlexGangitano, @Marcia_Brown9 and @dlippman.

— “Trump intervened in January and tapped his longtime supporter Meredith O’Rourke to stabilize the Kennedy Center’s fundraising operation, in a move that effectively sidelined senior vice president Lisa Dale, according to three current and one former employee.”

— “O’Rourke is also in charge of fundraising for the new White House ballroom and helped raise the money to replace the Rose Garden with a paved patio.”

MIDTERM MONEY: “Artificial intelligence startup Anthropic announced Thursday that it is donating $20 million to Public First Action, a political action committee set up to support candidates who favor AI regulations in the midterm elections,” our Brendon Bordelon reported Thursday.

— “Anthropic’s $20-million infusion into Public First, a 501(c)(4), comes days after an AI industry super PAC, Leading the Future, announced it has so far raised $125 million. Leading the Future aims to support AI-industry friendly candidates, and its donors include venture capitalist firm Andreessen Horowitz, OpenAI President Greg Brockman and Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale.”

FOREIGN DONATIONS: American colleges and universities have so far reported receiving more than $5.2 billion in foreign gifts and contracts last year, the Trump administration disclosed Wednesday as it presses ahead with investigations into four schools’ foreign ties, our Juan Perez Jr. reports in Morning Education.

The latest available numbers in the Education Department’s new foreign funding reporting portal now reflect approximately $67.6 billion in total foreign funding that institutions have reported receiving since 1986, Juan adds.

— But, but but: D.C. is already a deep-blue city. “‘Why don’t we have a lib Butterworth’s?’ Er... you mean like every other restaurant and coffee shop in DC?” White House deputy press secretary Abigail Jackson said on X.

— “The online report, titled ‘Saving America by Saving the Family: A Foundation for the Next 250 Years,’ published Jan. 8 by The Heritage Foundation, lays out ways the group says the United States can ‘restore the family home,’ including through monetarily incentivizing couples to have children and stay married, among other efforts,” Perez reports.

— The marriage bootcamps would “cover topics like communication, money management and conflict resolution for ‘cohabiting couples with children.’”

— “The successful completion of the program would conclude with couples ‘ready to walk down the aisle at a communal wedding,’ the report states, and a potential $5,000 monetary incentive − funded by foundations or private donors − for couples to get married. Additionally, newlyweds would leave with a mentor couple to guide them through marriage following the wedding.”

title: Trump tariffs still driving major business
body_text:
TARIFF BOOM CONTINUES: We’re still learning more about who has lobbied up for help navigating the Trump administration’s tariff whiplash as disclosures file in ahead of next week’s Q2 deadline. Kraft Heinz , whose Maxwell House and Gevalia would be hit hard by new duties on coffee beans, retained WilmerHale to lobby on tariffs beginning on May 1, according to a disclosure filing.

— The hire came more than a month before President Donald Trump upped the ante for coffee tariffs even further by threatening a 50 percent tariff on all imports from Brazil, the supplier of coffee beans to the U.S. Rob Lehman , a former chief of staff to Rob Portman (R-Ohio) during his time in Congress and at USTR, is working on the account.

— Therabody , which makes massage guns, brought on its second lobbying firm in as many months. Steptoe ’s Kevin Garvey , who served as chief of staff to former U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer during the first Trump administration, will represent the company before his former agency, according to a disclosure filing. Therabody previously hired Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg in May — the company’s first-ever federal lobbyists.

— APCO ’s Felicia Pullam , who served as executive director of the Office of Trade Relations at Customs and Border Protection during the Biden administration, has registered to lobby on trade policy for luxury outerwear retailer Canada Goose and Swedish furniture giant Ikea .

— The Haitian rum distillery Société du Rhum Barbancourt retained Corcoran Partners as a subcontractor to Hogan Lovells . Meanwhile in the auto world, American Defense International signed truck manufacturer Autocar to monitor the Trump administration’s Section 232 probe of severe duty truck parts and GrayRobinson registered to lobby for the Canadian Automobile Dealers Association as a subcontractor to Impact Public Affairs .

TGIF and welcome to PI . Send lobbying tips: Add me on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17 , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

WEATHER CHANNEL HIRES MICHAEL BEST: On the non-tariff lobbying front, the Weather Channel owner Weather Company has brought on Michael Best Strategies as its first outside lobbying firm since being spun off by IBM . The weather forecaster last month retained a team of former GOP aides to lobby on a bipartisan weather forecasting bill, access to NOAA weather data and the “role of private weather forecasting,” according to a disclosure filing.

— A House Science subcommittee held a hearing this week focused on using technology to improve weather forecasting in the wake of this month’s deadly floods in Texas. The hearing sparked debate about Trump’s thinning out of agencies like NOAA and push to shut down the National Weather Service. But Michael Best began working for the Weather Company prior to the tragedy.

— The week Michael Best was hired, Rep. Frank Lucas (R-Okla.) reintroduced legislation that would “fund the modernization of weather research programs, including for tornado warning and hurricane forecasting technologies,” and “increase NOAA’s access to forecasting data by expanding its authority to contract with the private sector,” E&E News’ Daniel Cusick reported at the time.

— Among those working on the account are Alex Angelson , a special assistant to Trump during his first term; Brittan Specht , a former counselor to House Speaker Mike Johnson and deputy chief of staff to former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy ; Jason Yaworske , another former Johnson and McCarthy aide who also worked in OMB during the first Trump administration; and Preston Hill , yet another McCarthy and Johnson alum.

AEROSPACE LOBBYIST MOVES TO CORNERSTONE: Veteran appropriations, aerospace and defense lobbyist Jessie Calio is joining the national and cybersecurity practice at Cornerstone Government Affairs .

— Calio was most recently at RTX , where she led approps and global government affairs operations. Before that Calio was the Air Force appropriations lead at Boeing (which is a Cornerstone client, as is the United Launch Alliance , the aerospace partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin ). She’s also worked for Textron , in the Pentagon’s legislative affairs office and for Rep. Michael Turner (R-Ohio).

EPA OFFICIAL HEADS TO PESTICIDES GROUP: EPA’s former liaison to agriculture and rural stakeholders has left the agency to join CropLife America , which represents pesticide producers. Venus Welch-White , who served as acting head of EPA’s Office of Agriculture and Rural Affairs until earlier this year, will be director of government relations for the trade group.

— The hire comes at a crucial moment for the pesticide industry, which has been working furiously during the Trump administration to push back against skepticism of their products by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other leaders of the “Make America Healthy Again” movement he inspired.

MORE NEW BUSINESS: Perrigo , which supplies store brand infant formula, hired Squire Patton Boggs to work on issues related to FDA oversight of the formula industry. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. met with formula makers including Perrigo weeks earlier, and announced in March that the federal government would conduct the first comprehensive review of baby formula and its ingredients in decades — a development welcomed by experts even as fears remain about Kennedy’s vilification of seed oils.

WHAT THE GOP CHATTERING CLASS IS READING: “In recent days, Republican circles in Washington have buzzed with speculation that former Trump administration official Katie Miller , an aide to Elon Musk and wife of one of the president’s closest advisers, and Musk have had a falling out,” Reuters’ Rachael Levy and Alexandra Ulmer report.

— But Miller sought to quash those rumors, which had been fueled by moves on social media like Musk unfollowing Katie Miller and her husband Stephen Miller , on X (Musk has since re-followed Stephen Miller, the architect of much of Trump’s domestic policy). She told Reuters in an interview that she still works for the Tesla and SpaceX CEO, “though she declined to describe her role or whether she serves as a spokesperson for him or his companies. ‘My paycheck still comes from him,’ she said.”

— “Late on Wednesday, after she spoke with Reuters, Miller issued a Musk-related press statement, apparently for the first time in around two weeks based on media reports of the statements and a statement received by Reuters.”

— Katie Miller, who followed Musk out of the Trump administration just before Musk’s dramatic split with the president, also removed a photo of a SpaceX rocket from her X profile recently and had been firing off posts about her family in recent days, jolting the Beltway rumor mill. “With Musk recently parting ways with several top executives at his companies and the apparent split on X, three Republican sources told Reuters they suspected that Katie Miller had also split with Musk.”

Trump tariffs still driving major business

By CAITLIN OPRYSKO 

07/18/2025 06:50 PM EDT

Presented by

With Daniel Lippman

TARIFF BOOM CONTINUES: We’re still learning more about who has lobbied up for help navigating the Trump administration’s tariff whiplash as disclosures file in ahead of next week’s Q2 deadline. Kraft Heinz, whose Maxwell House and Gevalia would be hit hard by new duties on coffee beans, retained WilmerHale to lobby on tariffs beginning on May 1, according to a disclosure filing.

— The hire came more than a month before President Donald Trump upped the ante for coffee tariffs even further by threatening a 50 percent tariff on all imports from Brazil, the supplier of coffee beans to the U.S. Rob Lehman, a former chief of staff to Rob Portman (R-Ohio) during his time in Congress and at USTR, is working on the account.

— Therabody, which makes massage guns, brought on its second lobbying firm in as many months. Steptoe’s Kevin Garvey, who served as chief of staff to former U.S. Trade Representative Robert Lighthizer during the first Trump administration, will represent the company before his former agency, according to a disclosure filing. Therabody previously hired Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg in May — the company’s first-ever federal lobbyists.

— APCO’s Felicia Pullam, who served as executive director of the Office of Trade Relations at Customs and Border Protection during the Biden administration, has registered to lobby on trade policy for luxury outerwear retailer Canada Goose and Swedish furniture giant Ikea.

— The Haitian rum distillery Société du Rhum Barbancourt retained Corcoran Partners as a subcontractor to Hogan Lovells. Meanwhile in the auto world, American Defense International signed truck manufacturer Autocar to monitor the Trump administration’s Section 232 probe of severe duty truck parts and GrayRobinson registered to lobby for the Canadian Automobile Dealers Association as a subcontractor to Impact Public Affairs.

TGIF and welcome to PI. Send lobbying tips: Add me on Signal at caitlinoprysko.17, email me at [email protected], and be sure to follow me on X: @caitlinoprysko.

WEATHER CHANNEL HIRES MICHAEL BEST: On the non-tariff lobbying front, the Weather Channel owner Weather Company has brought on Michael Best Strategies as its first outside lobbying firm since being spun off by IBM. The weather forecaster last month retained a team of former GOP aides to lobby on a bipartisan weather forecasting bill, access to NOAA weather data and the “role of private weather forecasting,” according to a disclosure filing.

— A House Science subcommittee held a hearing this week focused on using technology to improve weather forecasting in the wake of this month’s deadly floods in Texas. The hearing sparked debate about Trump’s thinning out of agencies like NOAA and push to shut down the National Weather Service. But Michael Best began working for the Weather Company prior to the tragedy.

— The week Michael Best was hired, Rep. Frank Lucas (R-Okla.) reintroduced legislation that would “fund the modernization of weather research programs, including for tornado warning and hurricane forecasting technologies,” and “increase NOAA’s access to forecasting data by expanding its authority to contract with the private sector,” E&E News’ Daniel Cusick reported at the time.

— Among those working on the account are Alex Angelson, a special assistant to Trump during his first term; Brittan Specht, a former counselor to House Speaker Mike Johnson and deputy chief of staff to former House Speaker Kevin McCarthy; Jason Yaworske, another former Johnson and McCarthy aide who also worked in OMB during the first Trump administration; and Preston Hill, yet another McCarthy and Johnson alum.

AEROSPACE LOBBYIST MOVES TO CORNERSTONE: Veteran appropriations, aerospace and defense lobbyist Jessie Calio is joining the national and cybersecurity practice at Cornerstone Government Affairs.

— Calio was most recently at RTX, where she led approps and global government affairs operations. Before that Calio was the Air Force appropriations lead at Boeing (which is a Cornerstone client, as is the United Launch Alliance, the aerospace partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin). She’s also worked for Textron, in the Pentagon’s legislative affairs office and for Rep. Michael Turner (R-Ohio).

EPA OFFICIAL HEADS TO PESTICIDES GROUP: EPA’s former liaison to agriculture and rural stakeholders has left the agency to join CropLife America, which represents pesticide producers. Venus Welch-White, who served as acting head of EPA’s Office of Agriculture and Rural Affairs until earlier this year, will be director of government relations for the trade group.

— The hire comes at a crucial moment for the pesticide industry, which has been working furiously during the Trump administration to push back against skepticism of their products by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and other leaders of the “Make America Healthy Again” movement he inspired.

MORE NEW BUSINESS: Perrigo, which supplies store brand infant formula, hired Squire Patton Boggs to work on issues related to FDA oversight of the formula industry. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. met with formula makers including Perrigo weeks earlier, and announced in March that the federal government would conduct the first comprehensive review of baby formula and its ingredients in decades — a development welcomed by experts even as fears remain about Kennedy’s vilification of seed oils.

WHAT THE GOP CHATTERING CLASS IS READING: “In recent days, Republican circles in Washington have buzzed with speculation that former Trump administration official Katie Miller, an aide to Elon Musk and wife of one of the president’s closest advisers, and Musk have had a falling out,” Reuters’ Rachael Levy and Alexandra Ulmer report.

— But Miller sought to quash those rumors, which had been fueled by moves on social media like Musk unfollowing Katie Miller and her husband Stephen Miller, on X (Musk has since re-followed Stephen Miller, the architect of much of Trump’s domestic policy). She told Reuters in an interview that she still works for the Tesla and SpaceX CEO, “though she declined to describe her role or whether she serves as a spokesperson for him or his companies. ‘My paycheck still comes from him,’ she said.”

— “Late on Wednesday, after she spoke with Reuters, Miller issued a Musk-related press statement, apparently for the first time in around two weeks based on media reports of the statements and a statement received by Reuters.”

— Katie Miller, who followed Musk out of the Trump administration just before Musk’s dramatic split with the president, also removed a photo of a SpaceX rocket from her X profile recently and had been firing off posts about her family in recent days, jolting the Beltway rumor mill. “With Musk recently parting ways with several top executives at his companies and the apparent split on X, three Republican sources told Reuters they suspected that Katie Miller had also split with Musk.”
