— “The political battle over the anti-obesity drugs is reaching a crescendo in Washington after a yearslong supply shortage sparked by historic demand. From 2022 to 2024, cheaper copycat versions filled the void. But now that supplies have recovered, brand-name companies are pressing federal officials to clamp down on those less expensive versions, known as compounded drugs.”

— “Separately, the drug industry is lobbying to repeal a 20-year-old law prohibiting Medicare from covering weight-loss drugs. Trump administration officials have cited cost concerns in opposing such a move so far. But proponents say billions in upfront expenses would be more than offset over time as fewer Americans face chronic conditions exacerbated by obesity.”

— “In the first quarter of 2025, Ozempic and Wegovy’s maker, Novo Nordisk, spent more than $3 million on lobbying. So did Eli Lilly, which makes the weight-loss drug Zepbound and Mounjaro, a similar drug tailored to diabetes patients. Together, the two companies hired more than 10 lobbying firms, including top Washington shops Avoq, Holland & Knight and Williams and Jensen, according to a POLITICO review of lobbying records.”

— “Hims, the prominent telehealth company that sells a copycat drug, also hired lobbyists, and competitor Ivim Health has tapped Sean Spicer, the former Trump administration press secretary, to serve as a Washington spokesperson. Both sell weight-loss drugs.”

FIRST IN PI — FORMER TRUMP LAWYER HANGS A SHINGLE: Another one of President Donald Trump ’s personal attorneys is jumping into lobbying. Jim Trusty and veteran gaming attorney Jeff Ifrah , who founded Ifrah Law — where Trusty has worked for the past eight years — are launching NexusOne Consulting , which will advise clients in the emerging technology space on changing tides for crypto, artificial intelligence and social media regulation.

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

DURBIN-MARSHALL CREDIT CARD MANDATES WILL HARM MILITARY FAMILIES The Defense Credit Union Council is sounding the alarm on the Durbin–Marshall credit card mandates. This proposal would increase fraud risk, restrict access to credit, eliminate rewards, and hand a massive windfall to corporate mega-retailers at the expense of consumers, small businesses, and community financial institutions. DCUC STANDS FIRMLY OPPOSED —OUR MILITARY AND THEIR FAMILIES DESERVE BETTER!

— Trusty helped steer Trump’s D.C.-based legal team between presidencies, including representing Trump during special counsel Jack Smith ’s classified documents probe and the investigation into Trump’s alleged efforts to subvert the 2020 election. Trusty withdrew from Trump’s legal team following Trump’s 2023 indictment in the documents case which — like the election obstruction case — has since been dismissed. Evan Corcoran , another veteran of Trump’s legal teams, now works at Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck .

— Ifrah is a former federal prosecutor who has become a go-to attorney for the gaming industry and cases involving sports betting. He also helped launch the gaming industry group iDevelopment and Economic Association . In an interview, Ifrah said that after Trump’s election win in November, he began batting around the question of “was there something to do with the fact that we now had a former client in the White House?”

— The idea for NexusOne is “to help our clients who are in the crypto AI and digital space, actually leverage the contacts that we may have in the White House, the executive branch, and hope that they can have a seat at the table as policy accelerates,” Ifrah said, pointing to the Trump administration’s retreat from the aggressive crypto enforcement posture of the Biden era (which Ifrah said had shuttered many of the crypto clients his firm worked for previously) and its promises to enact landmark AI policy.

— “It seemed like there was an opportunity there to really represent our clients in a way that was different than how we represented them before,” which until recently had been in a defensive or reactive posture rather than proactive, he added. In addition to crypto and AI, the firm expects to work on issues related to drones, prediction markets, data privacy and social media companies, according to Ifrah.

— Ross Branson , a lobbyist at Saildrone who served in the Commerce Department during the first Trump administration, will also join the new firm as managing director.

Happy Monday and welcome to PI. Hope you’re all recovered from the weekend’s festivities. Send tips: You can add me on Signal , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

TOP JOHNSON AIDE HEADS TO JENNER: Ashley Callen , the former general counsel to House Speaker Mike Johnson , is joining Jenner & Block as a partner, where she’ll co-chair the law firm’s congressional investigations practice and work with Jenner’s government controversies and public policy litigation practice — just as the firm is experiencing a bit of a government controversy itself.

— Jenner & Block is one of a handful of white shoe law firms that has fought back against the Trump administration’s efforts to punish them via restrictive executive orders. Jenner & Block drew Trump’s ire for hiring an attorney who previously worked for special counsel Robert Mueller and because of its DEI policies. Jenner was one of about a dozen top law firms identified by the administration as part of a sweeping retaliation campaign .

— While other Big Law firms struck deals with Trump to provide almost $1 billion in pro bono legal services for causes supported by Trump in exchange for being spared, Jenner sued the administration last month. In oral arguments today, the firm asked a federal judge to permanently block Trump’s executive order .

— In a statement, Jenner co-managing partners Ishan Bhabha and Randy Mehrberg lauded Callen as a “deeply experienced strategist in navigating government investigations” — and appeared to try and head off questions about the timing of her hiring. “Her insights into the inner workings of Congress are valuable additions to our team, which is why Jenner identified Ashley as a top recruit more than six months ago,” they said.

— Before serving in Johnson’s office, Callen worked for House Majority Leader Steve Scalise and spent a decade-and-a-half working in other key oversight roles on the Hill, including for the House Oversight and Judiciary committees and on key issues, including the Trump impeachments and oversight of the Covid-19 response.

SPEAKING OF TRUMP’S TARGETS: “After weeks of witnessing the administration freeze billions in federal funding, demand changes to policies and begin investigations, a broad coalition of university leaders publicly opposing those moves is taking root ,” The New York Times ’ Stephanie Saul and Alan Blinder report. “The most visible evidence yet was a statement last week signed by more than 400 campus leaders opposing what they saw as the administration’s assault on academia.”

— “Although organizations of colleges and administrators regularly conduct meetings on a wide range of issues, the statement by the American Association of Colleges and Universities was an unusual show of unity considering the wide cross-section of interests it included: Ivy League institutions and community colleges, public flagship schools and Jesuit universities, regional schools and historically Black colleges.”

— Amid the pressure from Trump, 10 schools “that have been singled out by the administration for scrutiny spent a combined $2.8 million lobbying the federal government in the first three months of 2025, which is more than those institutions spent in any quarter at least since 2008,” the Times’ Steven Rich and Vimal Patel found.

DAVIDS TAKE ON TRUMP TARIFFS WHILE GOLIATHS LOOK ON: “Nearly four weeks into a costly global trade war with no end in sight, Mr. Trump is facing a barrage of lawsuits from state officials, small businesses and even once-allied political groups , all contending that the president cannot sidestep Congress and tax virtually any import at levels to his liking,” per NYT’s Tony Romm .

— “The lawsuits carry great significance, not just because the tariffs have roiled financial markets and threatened to plunge the United States into a recession. The legal challenges also stand to test Mr. Trump’s claims of expansive presidential power, while illustrating the difficult calculation that his opponents face in deciding whether to fight back and risk retribution.”

— “None of the lawsuits filed this month are supported by major business lobbying groups, even though many organizations — including the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the Business Roundtable — have been sharply critical of the president’s tariffs and lobbied to lessen their impact.”

— “The chamber privately debated bringing a lawsuit, but ultimately decided it was ‘not the best course of action at this time,’ said Neil Bradley , the executive vice president of the group. … Instead, the battle has been left to a scattered yet growing roster of litigants,” including the heads of small toy company, board game, paper and clothing companies, and officials from more than a dozen blue states.

ALSO HANGING A SHINGLE: Matt Lee-Ashley has launched Foreground Strategy , which will provide organizations on policy, messaging, crisis management and government affairs strategies drawing in part on Lee-Ashley’s time in the Biden White House, where he served as chief of staff and director of policy and programs in the Council on Environmental Quality.

— Lee-Ashley is an Interior Department and Ken Salazar alum and was a senior fellow at the progressive think tank Center for American Progress before joining the Biden administration. He said in an email that he expects the new firm’s clients to include a mixture of climate, clean energy and outdoor-related nonprofits, philanthropies and businesses.

— “The core idea behind the new firm (and its name) is that in our cluttered political landscape, you need to be able [to] lift a problem — and a solution — into the foreground,” he said. “You don’t need deep pockets to do it, but you do need to develop a crisp idea, a clear message, and a smart and effective plan of action.”

IF THESE WALL STREETS COULD TALK: “Countries big and small are turning to Wall Street banks for guidance on how to navigate Trump’s global trade war,” The Wall Street Journal ’s Alexander Saeedy and AnnaMaria Andriotis report. Leaders from South Africa, France, Japan and Saudi Arabia are among those who have sought the counsel of Goldman Sachs in recent weeks, per WSJ.

— “Bankers have advised that negotiations with the Trump administration could be affected by issues that have nothing to do with trade and might require political or symbolic concessions to the White House.”

— “Wall Street’s biggest banks advise corporate clients on all manner of business, from mergers, IPOs and restructurings to major capital projects. They also regularly provide guidance to foreign governments, and talks have accelerated and become more urgent with Trump’s return to the White House.”

ROARING INTO TOWN: WSJ’s Maggie Severns profiled Ches McDowell , the 35-year-old North Carolina lobbyist bringing Checkmate Government Relations to Washington thanks to his friendship, forged through a love of hunting, with Donald Trump Jr. — and subsequently with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr .

— Instead of a resume of former government roles, McDowell is “parlaying his background as a self-described government skeptic, who made his children baby food out of dandelion root and bear meat he hunted himself in an effort to avoid additives, into a power broker for the new administration where Kennedy, the health secretary, is reconsidering the role of pharmaceuticals and food ingredients,” Severns writes.

— McDowell — whose brother Rep. Addison McDowell was just elected to Congress — has since hired one of Kennedy’s nephews ( Jackson Hines ) as well as the son of Trump’s former campaign co-chair ( Chris LaCivita Jr. ). Checkmate, whose clients include Eli Lilly , Novo Nordisk , the University of North Carolina and the Sports Betting Alliance , is also one of several Trump-aligned firms heavily leaning on being among the “regular guys” on K Street.

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

CONGRESS MUST REJECT DURBIN–MARSHALL

The Defense Credit Union Council is sounding the alarm on the Durbin–Marshall credit card mandates. This proposal would increase fraud risk, eliminate rewards programs, restrict access to credit, and hand a massive windfall to mega-retailers at the expense of consumers, small businesses, and community financial institutions. “This repeats the same mistakes consumers already paid for,” warns DCUC President & CEO Anthony Hernandez. A one-size-fits-all rewrite of the payments system would weaken fraud protections and hit servicemembers, veterans, and working families hardest. DCUC STRONGLY OPPOSES THIS BILL AND URGES ACTION TO SAFEGUARD THOSE WHO SERVE!

Jobs report

— Sam Beaver has joined the Brewers Association as a federal government affairs manager. He was most recently director of government relations at the National Association of Manufacturers and is a Senate Finance and John Cornyn alum.

— Jason Levine has joined the Crohn’s & Colitis Foundation as vice president of advocacy, overseeing their federal and state portfolios. Levine was most recently director of the Office of Governmental Affairs, Policy and Strategic Planning at the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration and is a Consumer Product Safety Commission, Center for Auto Safety and OPM alum.

— Asad Ramzanali is joining the Vanderbilt Policy Accelerator as director of AI and tech policy. He previously was special assistant to the president and chief of staff and deputy director of strategy for the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy in the Biden White House.

— Samantha Heyrich is now policy communications manager at Capital One . She previously was vice president at Black Rock Group and is a Trump Treasury and Pat Toomey alum.

— Hannah Morrow is joining SMI as a director. She was most recently government relations director for defense programs at Saildrone and is a House GOP alum.

— Emma Peters has joined the National Venture Capital Association as manager of government affairs. She was previously a grassroots manager at Engine .

— Cambridge Global Advisors has hired Jake Braun as its CEO. He was previously acting principal deputy national cyber director in the White House Office of the National Cyber Director. CGA is also adding former CISA Deputy Director Nitin Natarajan ; Jeff Greene , the former CISA executive assistant director for cybersecurity; Ret. Vice Adm. Paul Thomas , former deputy commandant for Mission Support at the U.S. Coast Guard; Seeyew Mo , former assistant national cyber director for Cyber Workforce, Education, and Economic Advancement at ONCD; and Analiese Wagner , former cyber policy adviser at ONCD.

body_text:
FIRST IN PI — USAGM HIRES GOVERNMENT RELATIONS FIRM FOR AGENCY AUDIT: The U.S. Agency for Global Media, under the direction of senior adviser Kari Lake , recently gave a sole-source $250,000 contract to the law firm Ragnar Group for “grantee monitoring” and “program consulting support” — an echo of a similar contract the agency struck during the first Trump administration that was criticized by the Biden administration State Department inspector general, Daniel reports.

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

DURBIN-MARSHALL CREDIT CARD MANDATES WILL HARM MILITARY FAMILIES The Defense Credit Union Council is sounding the alarm on the Durbin–Marshall credit card mandates. This proposal would increase fraud risk, restrict access to credit, eliminate rewards, and hand a massive windfall to corporate mega-retailers at the expense of consumers, small businesses, and community financial institutions. DCUC STANDS FIRMLY OPPOSED —OUR MILITARY AND THEIR FAMILIES DESERVE BETTER!

— The Ragnar Group was started by Robert Wasinger and Mike Andrews . Wasinger previously was White House liaison at the State Department in the first Trump administration and chief of staff to former Sen. Sam Brownback (R-Kan.). Andrews previously was staff director and chief counsel for the Senate Committee on Indian Affairs, a prosecutor in Arizona and a senior executive at DHS and HUD.

— The firm’s website says it provides consulting on a range of services, including legislative and executive branch strategy, legal support and business development. It also says it specializes in a range of fields, including sports law, energy and environmental issues, health care, agriculture and government contracting.

— As the Trump administration tries to scale back USAGM, it awarded the four-month contract to Ragnar Group on April 18. While the firm does say it provides “oversight, compliance and financial audit expertise to state and federal agencies,” the USAGM contract is the only time it’s secured a federal contract, according to a USASpending.gov record search .

— “As was suggested by members of Congress, a need for an expeditious and qualified audit became clear,” USAGM said in a statement to PI. “The U.S. Agency for Global Media used a Justification for Other Than Full and Open Competition (JOFOC) under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold to urgently procure audit and compliance services. This was done at an extremely low cost to the taxpayer and we look forward to receiving the results of the work to share with the American people.”

— Lake added in a text message that “most audits of this type involving the govt. cost millions and we are proud to have negotiated a cap of $250K (max they can charge us) to save the taxpayer money. And a reminder, this audit came about it because it was Congressionally advised that we audit the agency.”

— She has railed against some of USAGM’s grantees, called USAGM in its current form “unsalvageable” and tried to terminate all of its grant agreements , which has led to battles in the courts.

— Toward the end of the first Trump administration, USAGM hired McGuireWoods for a series of internal audits, which led to an IG investigation during the Biden administration that found “some of the items requested by USAGM constituted waste, because they were duplicative of existing resources and involved the payment of billable hours far in excess of the salary of federal employees who can perform the same work.”

— Wasinger was at McGuireWoods during that time, according to his LegiStorm profile, but he didn’t respond to a question about whether he had worked on the USAGM project while there.

— In a statement, a spokesperson for the Ragnar Group told PI that the firm “brings unique expertise to the Trump Administration’s critical work identifying the rampant waste, fraud and abuse that has undermined our government’s efficiency and credibility for many years.”

— “The agency’s principals have been deeply … engaged in this work for decades, as staffers on the Hill, in senior roles within federal agencies, and as outside consultants hired on previous government contracts. They founded Ragnar Group in February to support clients in the public and private sector that are excited to advance President Trump’s agenda and deliver the change that the American people voted for resoundingly.”

Happy Wednesday and welcome to PI , where we want to hear your assessment of Trump’s first 100 days — you can be as candid as you want, we’ll keep you anonymous. You can add me on Signal , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

BUSINESS ROUNDTABLE TAPS NEW POLICY LEAD : The Business Roundtable has promoted Matt Sonnesyn to oversee the business executives group’s policy team as senior vice president of policy. Sonnesyn first joined BRT as a research director in 2012, and he most recently served as vice president for infrastructure, energy and environment. He previously spent more than a decade working for former Sen. Lamar Alexander (R-Tenn.), including as chief of staff.

A NEW ALLIANCE IN SILICON VALLEY: “App makers Meta Platforms Inc. , Spotify Technology SA and Match Group Inc. are girding for a high-stakes political battle with the world’s two dominant smartphone platforms over who should take responsibility for verifying users’ ages,” Bloomberg ’s Emily Birnbaum reports.

— They’re staking out their territory with a new coalition “to take on Apple Inc. and Alphabet Inc. as legislation to require age verification gains momentum amid rising public concern over minors’ online access to inappropriate material.”

— “The Coalition for a Competitive Mobile Experience also will press app makers’ long-simmering grievances that the iPhone and Android platforms and their app stores unfairly discriminate against competing software, app and hardware creators. The group will lobby federal and state policymakers to enact legislation cracking down on the smartphone companies’ business practices, as well as aid the Justice Department in its cases against Apple and Google.”

— “Some members of the coalition, such as smartwatch maker Garmin Ltd. , are focused on ensuring Apple and Google products work effectively with technology and apps from rival companies.”

PHARMA CHIPS AWAY AT PBMS: “Trump’s second term has upended the business of K Street, with many industries feeling left in the cold. An exception: the drug industry’s campaign against so-called middlemen , or pharmacy-benefit managers, such as those owned by CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group, which manage prescription-drug benefits for health insurers,” The Wall Street Journal ’s Josh Dawsey , Kristina Peterson and Maggie Severns write.

ACPA’S LAST STAND: The renewable energy industry’s top trade group fanned out across the Hill today for a lobbying blitz to preserve the Inflation Reduction Act’s suite of clean energy tax incentives, E&E News’ Nico Portuondo reports, but unlike your typical industry fly-in, “it won’t be high-level executives who will be making the case for the climate law” on behalf of members of the American Clean Power Association .

— “More than 160 ‘front-line workers’ from across the renewable energy supply chain — including solar panel installers, wind turbine manufacturers and electrical engineers — will meet with members of Congress to outline the job-creating impacts of clean energy projects bolstered by the Inflation Reduction Act.”

— The fly-in “comes as Republicans work to finalize the tax portions of their party-line megabill before a committee vote as soon as next week. Congressional leaders and the administration are working to decide what parts of the climate bill survive, get tweaked or die. … House Ways and Means Chair Jason Smith (R-Mo.) has said the fate of the Inflation Reduction Act is one of a few sticking points that the committee still has to parse out.”

— Meanwhile, the Koch-backed Americans for Prosperity launched its own salvo against the IRA tax credits with a new ad buy blasting the incentives as “reckless spending on green fantasies.”

— “Eliminating Joe Biden ‘s Green New Deal helps pay for President Trump’s tax cuts,” the group argued in a 30-second spot that will run within the Beltway .

Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa), Roy Blunt of the Bipartisan Policy Center and Husch Blackwell Strategies , Emil Kakkis of Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical , Scott Schell of Cognizant , Diogo Rau of Eli Lilly and Robert Schmidt of the Carlyle Group .

— And last night at Butterworth ’s for a reception celebrating the launch of the Ragnar Group, per a tipster: Rob Wasinger and Mike Andrews of Ragnar Group, Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kan.), Reps. Jack Bergman (R-Mich.), Tracey Mann (R-Kan.), FCC Chair Brendan Carr , Pentagon general counsel nominee Earl Matthews , Josh Lynch of Verizon , Matt Flynn of Steptoe , Randy Russell and Mora Namdar of USAGM, Brent Robertson of Marshall’s office, Wyatt Toehlke of the State Department, Kevin Salinger of the Treasury Department, Erik Noble of the Commerce Department, Erik Finman of Future PAC and Steve Bannon .

A message from the Defense Credit Union Council:

CONGRESS MUST REJECT DURBIN–MARSHALL

The Defense Credit Union Council is sounding the alarm on the Durbin–Marshall credit card mandates. This proposal would increase fraud risk, eliminate rewards programs, restrict access to credit, and hand a massive windfall to mega-retailers at the expense of consumers, small businesses, and community financial institutions. “This repeats the same mistakes consumers already paid for,” warns DCUC President & CEO Anthony Hernandez. A one-size-fits-all rewrite of the payments system would weaken fraud protections and hit servicemembers, veterans, and working families hardest. DCUC STRONGLY OPPOSES THIS BILL AND URGES ACTION TO SAFEGUARD THOSE WHO SERVE!

Jobs report

— Mannar Hanna has joined APCO as a senior director of government relations. He was previously former general counsel to Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.).

— Franklin Davis will be head of federal affairs at the American Beverage Association . He was previously vice president of federal government relations for the trade group.

— Daria Dudzinski is joining the Real Estate Technology & Transformation Center , an affiliate of the National Multifamily Housing Council , as director of advocacy. She was most recently a political representative at the National Association of Realtors .

— Mindset has added Sarah Alexander and Gary Rubin as senior directors. Alexander was most recently energy and coastal policy adviser to Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.). Rubin was most recently deputy head of regulatory interpretations at Wells Fargo .

— Alexandra de Hoop Scheffer will be the next president of the German Marshall Fund . She was most recently GMF’s senior vice president for geostrategy and acting president.

— Brett Hart is joining the Rockefeller Foundation ‘s Board of Trustees. He is the president of United Airlines and an alum of the Clinton administration.

— Alan Inouye is retiring as interim associate executive director of the American Library Association , to be succeeded by Lisa Varga . She previously was executive director of the Virginia Library Association .

— Inseparable has added Cara Cheevers as vice president of coverage policy, Arpit Jain as vice president of finance, Abbie Hodgson and Laurie Roberts as senior directors of state affairs, Julianne Hopper and Shannon Hoofman as policy and advocacy managers, and Imogen Bohen as policy and advocacy coordinator.

— Cora Swanson will lead Viewpoint Media following its spinoff from Uplift Campaigns ’ media buying operation, along with Jamie Patton , Andy Barr , Lili McFarlane , Ann Bremer and Sam Almy .

— Ellie Hockenbury is joining Targeted Victory as a managing director on its public affairs team. She previously was deputy executive director and comms director for the California GOP, and is an RNC and RSLC alum.

title: The Chamber’s tariff exemption wish list
body_text:
CHAMBER LAYS OUT ITS TARIFF BOUNDARIES: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce , which counts some of the world’s biggest companies among its members, is pressing the White House to lay down some road rules to trigger automatic exclusions for certain goods and importers from the so-called reciprocal tariffs President Donald Trump rolled out — and then rolled back — last month.

— Though the business lobby wants to ultimately see zero-for-zero tariff reciprocity and reduced non-tariff trade barriers, Chamber President Suzanne Clark argued in a letter today that even if it only takes weeks or months to negotiate dozens of new trade agreements with other countries, “many small businesses will suffer irreparable harm” because of the administration’s policies.

— “We must work together to avoid a recession and to realize America’s economic potential,” Clark said in a statement, adding that Trump “has no greater ally than the Chamber on our shared pro-growth priorities.”

— To help alleviate that, Clark asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent , Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer in the letter to introduce an “automatic” exemption from tariffs for “any small business importer,” given many small businesses’ slim margins and lack of ability to quickly pivot their supply chains.

— The group is also calling for automatic tariff exclusions for “all products that cannot be produced in the U.S. or are not readily available from domestic sources,” citing items like coffee, bananas, cocoa and certain minerals, as well as “bespoke industrial inputs critical to American manufacturers.”

— Beyond those automatic triggers, the Chamber wants the Trump administration to set up a formal process through which businesses can petition for exemptions if they’re able to demonstrate “significant risks” to their U.S. workforce caused by the tariffs.

— The White House’s exemption process thus far has been opaque, sparking complaints from some industry groups. Trump has issued broad carveouts (for now) for products like semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, lumber, critical minerals and energy and granted one-off reprieves for products like consumer tech and auto parts, telling reporters he’ll go off “instinct” for future exemptions.

— The tech-backed small business group Connected Commerce Council just wrapped up its own fly-in, with representatives from 30 small businesses huddling with staff from Vice President JD Vance ’s office and the White House’s Office of Science and Technology Policy and Domestic Policy Council. It also held member-level meetings with Sens. Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.) and Deb Fischer (R-Neb.), according to the council. The talks focused on data privacy legislation and the use of artificial intelligence by small businesses.

— Leaders from the alternative investments industry are also in town for a fly-in organized by the Institute for Portfolio Alternatives , which advocates for expanded investment in alternative assets such as real estate or private equity.

— The industry has more than 150 meetings on the books this week — including with Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott (R-S.C.), Senate Finance ranking member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and House tax writers Vern Buchanan (R-Fla.) and Terri Sewell (D-Ala.) — to push for the extension of the opportunity zone tax incentive set to expire and for tweaks to the definition of an “accredited investor.”

A fund backed by Abu Dhabi, he said, would be making a $2 billion business deal using the Trump firm’s digital coins ,” according to The New York Times’ David Yaffe-Bellany .

— Zach Witkoff , the son of Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff and “a founder of the Trump family crypto firm, World Liberty Financial , revealed that a so-called stablecoin developed by the firm would be used to complete the transaction between the state-backed Emirati investment firm MGX and Binance , the largest crypto exchange in the world. Virtually every detail of Mr. Witkoff’s announcement, made during a conference panel with [ Eric Trump ], contained a conflict of interest.”

— Prior to leading the CHC, Colón-Rivera worked in the Commerce Department and Census Bureau under former President Joe Biden and spent more than a decade on the Hill working for former Sens. Bob Menendez (D-N.J.) and Ben Cardin (D-Md.) and the late Rep. Alcee Hastings (D-Fla.).

Morgan McGarvey (R-Ky.), Chris Smith and Jessica Carter of Ford, Chris Cerone of Novelis , Dex Battista of Magna , Emily Buckman of the American Farm Bureau Federation , John Bozzella of the Alliance For Automotive Innovation and staffers for Kentucky’s congressional delegation.

title: Panama Maritime Authority hires Checkmate
body_text:
FIRST IN PI: The entity that oversees Panama’s shipping registry and ports has added new lobbying firepower with ties to President Donald Trump as he doubles down on a pressure campaign targeting the vital shipping passage.

— The Panama Maritime Authority has hired Checkmate Government Relations — the firm founded by Ches McDowell , a close friend of Donald Trump Jr. and the brother of first-term Rep. Addison McDowell (R-N.C.) — to advise the organization on engaging with the Trump administration. The maritime authority is currently reviewing a March deal for a group of investors, including BlackRock , to acquire control of two key ports near the Panama Canal from Hong Kong-based CK Hutchinson .

— “The United States and Panama have a long and historically collaborative relationship,” McDowell told PI in a statement. “We look forward to helping ensure that relationship continues in a way that strengthens both nations.”

— In February, Vinson & Elkins , the longtime law firm for the entity that controls the passageway, registered to advise the Panama Canal Authority on political strategy in Washington. Days earlier, Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino’s government staffed up on Trump-connected lobbyists in the wake of Trump’s threats to reclaim control over the canal, enlisting a team of lobbyists at BGR Group and VantageKnight that includes longtime Trump adviser David Urban .

— Trump began floating a takeover late last year, complaining that the canal had succumbed to Chinese influence and was overcharging American ships for their passage through the waterway. Mulino has rejected Trump’s calls to retake the canal, even as the Panamanian government moved to distance itself from China. NBC News reported in March that the White House had asked the Pentagon to draw up plans to retake the canal by force if deemed necessary.

— This past weekend, Trump demanded in a post on Truth Social that American military and commercial ships be allowed to pass through the Panama and Suez canals “free of charge” and wrote that he’d tasked Secretary of State Marco Rubio — who visited the canal earlier this year — to make that happen.

— Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also toured the canal while he was in Panama in April, and the Pentagon announced a memorandum of understanding between the U.S. and Panama that it said “would provide a framework for U.S. warships and auxiliary ships to travel ‘first and free’ through the canal.”

— In response to Trump’s posts last weekend, Mulino wrote on X that the “transits and costs of all vessels through our Canal” are set by the autonomous Panama Canal Authority.

— The Panama Maritime Authority is the second foreign client signed by Checkmate this year. In February, the Washington newcomers helped Canadian premiers coordinate a White House visit to discuss Trump’s tariff and annexation threats.

NEW TARIFF BUSINESS: Sorini, Samet & Associates has signed a trio of prominent retail goods brands for tariff work as uncertainty over the fate of Trump’s trade policies persists. The manufacturer of stainless steel Solo Stove firepits , the clothing retailer Reformation and the company behind enormously popular Stanley water bottles all retained Sorini to lobby on trade and tariff issues beginning this week, according to disclosure filings.

— It’s the first time any of the companies have hired federal lobbyists, and they’re not the only prominent retail brands that have turned to K Street for the first time to navigate tariff policy, recent disclosures show.

— Last month, popular pellet grill maker Traeger hired Sandler, Travis & Rosenberg to work on issues related to the administration’s steel tariffs. The grillmaker said on an earnings call this week that in addition to the steel tariffs, the vast majority of its grills are imported from China, while the rest are produced in Vietnam.

Also joining Lowell at the new firm are two associates poached from Winston & Strawn , the international firm where Lowell had been a partner since 2018.”

— “Lowell has had a long career representing high-profile political clients from both parties. Most recently, he was lead counsel for Hunter Biden in two criminal cases on federal gun and tax evasion charges. Biden was convicted of the gun charges and pleaded guilty to the tax changes before being pardoned by his father, President Joe Biden .”

(Barrack, who like Lowell’s client was acquitted, was confirmed this week as U.S. ambassador to Turkey.)

— “At the Pentagon, Mr. Trump is calling for a massive jump in spending, an extraordinary 13 percent increase, almost entirely through allocations in a Congressional budget reconciliation plan under consideration.”

— “The jump would happen while many other federal agencies would be slashed, in part to supercharge federal spending in two areas where SpaceX is positioned to profit: a vast missile defense system and space missions to Mars and the moon.”

— “SpaceX is already, by far, the largest recipient of Pentagon spending on existing military low-earth-orbit communications systems, and it gets the largest cut of Pentagon rocket launch contracts. Congressional approval for the plan to significantly expand this spending would be a giant win for Mr. Musk and SpaceX.”

— The report, which surveyed 300 Beltway political professionals in February, found that traditional news sources like national newspapers, cable and broadcast TV and local TV still reign supreme. — Nearly seven in 10 respondents said they’re on social media at least three times per week, while 64 percent listened to radio at least three times a week. Following an election in which podcasts became a crucial messaging platform for both presidential campaigns, 43 percent of respondents reported listening to those at least three times per week.

— Newer social media sites have yet to really break through, according to the survey: While 83 percent reported being on Meta -owned Facebook and 75 percent regularly using Meta-owned Instagram , those numbers plunged to 14 percent for Bluesky , 8 percent for Truth Social and 5 percent for Mastodon .

title: Akin hires Trump trade negotiator
body_text:
AKIN SNAGS TRUMP TRADE VETERAN: Kelly Ann Shaw , who served as one of President Donald Trump ’s top trade advisers during his first administration, has decamped from Hogan Lovells to join Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld as a partner in the lobbying practice.

— Shaw most recently co-led Hogan Lovells’ geopolitical risk and national security program. She joined the firm in 2020 from the White House, where she was a deputy assistant to the president for international economics and helped lead the administration’s negotiations for the phase one trade deal with China signed in 2020.

— Shaw said in an interview that she’s eager to advise Akin’s clients on “navigating what is the single-biggest shake up of the global trading system of my lifetime” and impart some of the wisdom that she learned from being at the negotiating table for dozens of trade deals over the years, but particularly under Trump.

— “I think that everyone has to accept a certain level of ambiguity and uncertainty. That’s part of the president’s calling card,” Shaw told PI. “When it comes to negotiations, you never quite know exactly where he stands, and having been a negotiator for him, I can say that that strategy is very helpful.” That unpredictability is less of an asset when you’re representing the business community, she conceded.

— Shaw also said she’d advise clients looking to engage with almost any White House — but especially Trump’s — that you get more bees with honey. “Instead of coming with a problem, come with an idea, and come with an idea that rows in the same direction, policywise, that the administration is going,” she said.

— Shaw’s arrival at Akin comes a matter of days after Clete Willems , her predecessor as one of Trump’s senior White House trade advisers , left the firm to take over global public policy at Netflix .

— Before joining the White House, Shaw was a Republican trade counsel for the House Ways and Means Committee, where she was the panel’s top lawyer for USMCA negotiations. She also spent six years at USTR in both Washington and Geneva.

Happy Monday and welcome to PI , where we’re just glad Journalism ended this weekend’s race on the podium, the way things have been going. Send other Kentucky Derby takeaways and lobbying tips. You can add me on Signal , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

ANNALS OF ETHICS: “ Tim Parlatore is a personal attorney and top adviser to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth . At the same time, he’s suing the Navy and defending private clients against the U.S. government,” Daniel and POLITICO ’s Josh Gerstein report.

— “Parlatore, who represented Donald Trump in a criminal case two years ago and rejoined the Navy Reserve in March to aid Hegseth, was recently tapped to coordinate the leak investigation that led to chaos at the Pentagon ,” and he “ was also reportedly in the Signal group with Hegseth’s wife and brother in which the Defense secretary shared details of a strike on Yemen.”

— “But despite Parlatore’s deep involvement at the Pentagon, he is pursuing litigation against the Navy. … While Parlatore insists his arrangement is above board, it’s highly unusual for a sitting top adviser for a Cabinet secretary to be working in the government while at the same time representing clients suing the government, or working for clients as they fight off the feds.”

SHEIN’S BET ON TRUMP: “Many companies have shamelessly courted President Donald Trump, hoping to curry favor with a uniquely transactional American leader, but few appear to have gone as far as Shein ,” Wired ’s Timothy McLaughlin reports.

— The company has had several high-ranking Trump officials on its payroll, such as FBI Director Kash Patel , deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche and even U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer , who in his former role at King & Spalding provided Shein “legal advice around international trade policy,” according to internal documents.

— Greer reportedly helped a Shein executive craft the response to a bipartisan congressional inquiry on Shein’s business practices — even as Greer testified publicly weeks later that China presented an “existential” threat to U.S. industries.

— “But despite the company’s overtures, Trump has dealt Shein a series of devastating blows since returning to office,” including placing steep tariffs on Chinese imports and moving to close the de minimis loophole so critical to Shein’s business model.

JUDGE BRUSHES BACK TRUMP WAR ON BIG LAW: “President Donald Trump’ s executive order that sought to punish the law firm Perkins Coie for working with Hillary Clinton and other Democrats is unconstitutional, ‘motivated by retaliation’ and cannot be enforced, a federal judge ruled ,” POLITICO ’s Daniel Barnes reports.

— “It marks the biggest setback so far for Trump’s campaign against law firms that have represented his political enemies — though key provisions of the orders have been blocked as four firms challenged them in court.” It’s the first of several pending final rulings in law firms’ legal challenges, but appeals are expected.

UNLIKELY UNBEDFELLOWS: “The Republican-led push to abolish the US estate tax has provoked opposition from a seemingly surprising source ,” according to Bloomberg ’s Steven Dennis and Ben Steverman : the “financial advisers the wealthy pay to manage their money and keep down their taxes.”

— “Many of the country’s richest families, who spend handsomely to lessen the tax burden on their heirs, have fought unsuccessfully for decades to repeal the 109-year-old levy. But industry group Finseca , which represents some 11,000 members including life insurance brokers and others who provide financial products and services, warns that many clients ultimately would be ill-served by an outright termination of the 40% tax.”

— That’s pitting the group against “more than 200 groups representing car dealers, farm interests, construction companies, funeral directors, plastics manufacturers, alcoholic beverage distributors, dude ranchers, and grocers that have lined up to back Senate Majority Leader John Thune ’s bid to repeal the estate tax .”

FIRST IN PI — LIBERAL GROUPS PUSH TO BLOCK JUDICIARY BILL: Three dozen left-leaning advocacy groups and labor organizations are calling on lawmakers to reject a bill that would gradually increase the size of the federal judiciary.

— The House Judiciary Committee approved the JUDGES Act in March , teeing it up for a floor vote. In a letter to lawmakers led by liberal judicial advocacy group Demand Justice , the progressive groups argued that supporting the measure now “violates both the intent and bipartisan spirit in which these kinds of bills have been considered and passed.”

— The JUDGES Act was initially the result of a bipartisan agreement last year that aimed to address understaffed courts by incrementally adding 66 new federal judgeships over the course of a decade. Former President Joe Biden vetoed the bill in January , accusing House Republicans of deliberately waiting until after the election to take up the bill, undermining its aims.

— While the signatories, which also included the AFL-CIO , Planned Parenthood Federation of America , SEIU , the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund and the National Association of Consumer Advocates , wrote that they “acknowledge the need for additional judgeships,” they pointed to Trump’s frequent attacks on the judiciary during his second term.

— “As President Trump and the administration pursue expanded executive powers that threaten our public services and civil rights, our district courts and district judges must remain an essential check on the other branches of our government,” they argued.

MEANWHILE, ACROSS THE POND: “The European Parliament has toughened its rules on lobbying more than two years after a cash-for-influence scandal that triggered one of the largest corruption investigations to hit the EU,” per POLITICO ’s Max Griera .

— Starting this month, “anyone entering the Parliament’s buildings to advocate on behalf of outside bodies has been forced to activate badges and register the purpose of their visit. The plan aims to keep tabs on who is talking to whom in the wake of what became known as ‘Qatargate’ ― named after one of the countries linked to allegedly offering cash and gifts in return for favors.”

— Lobbyists entering the Parliament will now have to activate their badges “every time they visit via a small terminal with badge readers at the entrances. That will require them to declare whether they are meeting an MEP or staff member or attending a parliamentary meeting or event taking place in the building, according to an email sent to all accredited lobbyists circulated last month.”

A NEW EV COALITION: More than a dozen fleet managers, charging companies and vehicle manufacturers are launching a coalition to defend a credit that’s received relatively little attention in the IRA fight: the credit for commercial electric vehicles, our friends at Morning Energy report.

— GOP lawmakers have largely eyed that credit, known as 45W, for elimination because it contains what they call the “leasing loophole” — through which the incentive intended for commercial fleets is being claimed by car manufacturers’ financing arms to make consumers’ EV leases cheaper.

— But the American Fleet Leadership Coalition is making the case to keep it, at least for businesses electrifying their fleets. Josh Green , the CEO of fleet manager Inspiration Mobility and founder of the new coalition, said it helps achieve GOP goals by reducing costs on fuel and maintenance for small businesses and supporting domestic manufacturing.

Abe Hamadeh (R-Ariz.) and Darrell Issa (R-Calif.), former Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin , Paraguayan President Santiago Pena , Ecuadorian Ambassador to the U.S. Pablo Zambrano Albuja , SEC Commissioner Mark Uyeda , Peninsula owner Robert Zarnegin , Caroline Wren and Ryan Coyne of Tactic Global, Bill Ackman of Pershing Square , Jane Fraser of Citigroup , Norm Brownstein of Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck , Rebecca Karabus of Treasury, Barry Sternlicht of Starwood Capital Group, Mark Holscher of Kirkland & Ellis , Robin Vince of Bank of New York Mellon , Jihan Wu of Bitdeer , Ryan Breslow of Bolt , Igor Tulchinsky of WorldQuant , Pandu Sjahrir of sovereign wealth fund Danantara , John Koudounis of Calamos Investments , Kevin Lu of Partners Group and producer John Penotti .

Jobs report

— The Energy and Commerce Committee has added Byron Brown as chief counsel for the Environment Subcommittee. He was most recently assistant general counsel for the American Chemistry Council and is a House, Senate, and EPA alum.

— Foley & Lardner ’s Nate Lacktman will be the new board chair for the American Telemedicine Association .

— Jeff Bozman has joined Gecko Robotics as head of government relations. He was previously a managing director at Anduril and is a House Armed Services alum.

— Jeffrey Hardin Lewis has joined Cozen O’Connor as a member in the transportation and trade group. He was most recently chief counsel in DOT’s Maritime Administration office.

— Garrett Berntsen is now managing director at Accenture Federal Services . He’s worked previously on data and AI issues at the State Department, National Security Council and Defense Department.

— Forterra has added Stephen Rubright as head of government affairs and John Mark Wilson as defense growth lead. Rubright previously headed government affairs and policy at Astellas . Wilson was previously with Applied Intuition and the National Security Council.

— Jasjit Vidwan has joined Mayer Brown as a partner in its intellectual property practice. He joins from ArentFox Schiff LLP .

— Renae Black has joined Duke Energy as vice president of policy and chief sustainability officer. Black most recently served as staff director for the Senate Energy & Natural Resources Committee.

— Becca Glover is now executive director of Virginia Gov. Glenn Youngkin ’s Spirit of Virginia PAC . She was previously deputy chief of staff for Youngkin and is a Trump Administration and Burr for Senate alum.

— Chandler Douglas is now special adviser to the assistant secretary of investment security at the Treasury Department. He previously was assistant vice president of government relations at Blackstone .

— Hannah Lepow is now senior counsel for regulatory affairs at NBCUniversal . She previously was legal adviser to FCC Commissioner Geoffrey Starks .

— Angela Hanks is joining The Century Foundation as chief of policy programs. She previously was associate director of external affairs at the CFPB.

— Eric Kohn is now CEO of America’s Future . He most recently was chief marketing officer of Empower Illinois and producer of the documentary “The Hong Konger.”

— Adam Talbot is launching Pilotboat Strategies , an executive and leadership communications firm. He is an Apple , West Wing Writers and Human Rights Campaign alum.

— Caitlin Kovalkoski is now a policy adviser at Arnold & Porter . She most recently was director of legislative and intergovernmental affairs for the Commerce Department’s International Trade Administration.

None.

body_text:
C SOMETHING, SAY SOMETHING: Financial officers and tax executives from nearly a dozen of the nation’s top retailers headed to the Hill today in an effort to stave off new limits on the state and local tax deduction for businesses that are being considered as congressional Republicans construct their reconciliation package.

— The fly-in, organized by the National Retail Federation , was set to include meetings with officials at the National Economic Council, Treasury and the White House’s public and legislative affairs offices, according to NRF, as well as staff for Senate Finance Chair Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Thom Tillis (R-N.C.) and Rep. Mike Kelly (R-Pa.).

— A cap on business SALT deductions (or C-SALT) appears likely to fall out of House Republicans’ final bill , as POLITICO ’s Benjamin Guggenheim and Meredith Lee Hill reported last week, though the business community isn’t resting on its laurels. The NRF was not one of the more than 300 trade associations that signed on to a Monday letter to lawmakers opposing C-SALT caps.

— Back in April, NRF wrote in a memo that capping C-SALT deductions “would effectively raise the business tax rate, undermining the competitive gains retailers have made” since the 2017 GOP tax law slashed the corporate rate and introduced a litany of tax breaks corporate America is now pushing to make permanent.

CASSIDY AIDE JOINS FAEGRE DRINKER: Barrett Tenbarge , who served as a top lawyer for Republicans on the Senate HELP Committee, is headed to Faegre Drinker Biddle & Reath as a partner with the government and regulatory group. Tenbarge most recently served as general counsel for Senate HELP Chair Bill Cassidy (R-La.) and before that was a senior counsel for the panel’s health subcommittee under Cassidy and former Chair Richard Burr (R-N.C.).

— Tenbarge will advise clients in the life sciences space or FDA-regulated industries like biopharmaceuticals, medical devices, food, dietary supplements and cosmetics. His hiring comes as HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. moves to upend the regulatory and public policy status quo for the food and health sectors.

Happy Tuesday and welcome to PI . What’s going on out there? Fill me in: You can add me on Signal , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

FIRST IN PI — MORE AIR COVER ON MEDICAID: Conservative nonprofits are coming to the defense of congressional Republicans as they face an onslaught from Democrats and allied outside groups over cutting Medicaid in order to help pay for Republicans’ reconciliation bill.

— The Center for a Free Economy is going up with a six-figure ad buy aimed at steeling Republicans’ resolve amid the attacks by lobbing criticism at Democratic health care policies, including highlighting the 95 percent excise tax on drug companies that refuse to negotiate with Medicare over the cost of their drugs as part of the Inflation Reduction Act.

— The 30-second spot will run on social media and streaming services within the Beltway throughout the reconciliation process. The ad argues that “you deserve the facts about how Democrats ruined your health care,” and points to Medicare premium increases while tying reduced Medicare spending — a result of the IRA’s drug pricing provisions — to the law’s incentives for boosting electric vehicle adoption.

— “The ad basically makes the point that they’re living in a glass house, but they don’t really get to make these existential claims on Medicaid,” said Ryan Ellis , CFE’s president, of the Democratic attacks. (Ellis is a lobbyist at Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld , where his clients include the drug lobby PhRMA , which donated more than $350,000 to CFE in 2023, according to tax returns.)

— CFE’s ad buy, which Ellis said could be expanded, comes as a number of other conservative groups have stepped in to provide backup for Republicans. The American Action Network , the dark money arm of the Congressional Leadership Fund , launched a seven-figure ad buy that will run in battleground districts praising House Republicans for tackling Medicare “waste, fraud and abuse,” Punchbowl reported this morning . That follows a similar ad blitz in March by the Republican Main Street Partnership .

DEMS PROTEST TRUMP CRYPTO VENTURES: “A joint meeting between the House Financial Services and Agriculture committees focused on cryptocurrency policy briefly descended into chaos Tuesday as Rep. Maxine Waters (D-Calif.) objected and walked out of the hearing, pointing to concerns over the Trump family’s digital asset businesses,” POLITICO ’s Jasper Goodman writes.

— “Waters said she objected ‘because of the corruption of the president of the United States and his ownership of crypto and his oversight of all the agencies.’” Some Democrats stayed at the roundtable to question witnesses “about landmark digital assets legislation that Republicans unveiled as a draft Monday,” even as they “still raised concerns about President Donald Trump .”

— Waters and the others who left the room held their own “shadow hearing” where they highlighted what they called “Trump’s crypto corruption,” while Financial Services Chair French Hill (R-Ark.) accused Waters of “undermining the opportunity for these two committees to engage in a conversation of vital importance to the American people.”

BROADCAST LOBBYIST HEADS TO SMITH FREE: Mike Mullen has left Empire Consulting Group , where he spent the past four years as a partner, to join the Smith Free Group as a senior vice president.

— Mullen previously served as vice president of government relations for the National Association of Broadcasters for a decade and a half, and before that he was a senior aide to former Rep. Mike Doyle (D-Pa.). Both NAB and Fox Corporation are expected to follow Mullen to the firm as clients.

ALSO FLYING IN: Fly-in season is in full swing, and this week will see another slew of trade associations and advocacy groups fanning out across the Hill. That includes a bipartisan delegation of nearly a dozen mayors, who are in town to promote the U.S. Conference of Mayors ’ reconciliation priorities . Those include avoiding Medicaid cuts, restoring and expanding the Child Tax Credit, preserving the tax exemption for municipal bonds and including housing initiatives.

— The delegation, led by conference President Andrew Ginther of Columbus, Ohio, also plans on bringing up the “the quick and damaging economic effects of tariffs on local communities” and broader issues like inflation and public safety.

— Small business owners and online creators with the Internet for Growth coalition will hit the Hill this week to talk data privacy and online ad targeting. The coalition is backed by the online advertising lobby, the Interactive Advertising Bureau , whose members include Meta and Google .

— The fly-in this week will include meetings with several key members of Congress including House Speaker Mike Johnson , Sens. Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), John Kennedy (R-La.) and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.) and Reps. Buddy Carter (R-Ga.), Celeste Maloy (R-Utah) and Carol Miller (R-W.Va.) to push for the protection of online targeted advertising in federal data privacy legislation.

— More than 120 fitness industry executives will also be in town for the Health & Fitness Association ’s annual summit. Industry leaders are slated to meet with more than 100 congressional offices to lobby for the PHIT Act, which would let people use pre-tax accounts like FSAs and HSAs to help pay for gym memberships, fitness classes or programs like youth sports leagues, and fitness equipment.

— Retired Col. Joe Funderburke has launched The Funderburke Group , a strategic advisory firm focused on national security, public policy, strategic planning and leadership development, Morning Defense reports. — Jana del-Cerro and Elyssa Kutner are joining DLA Piper ‘s national security and global trade practice as partners. Del-Cerro was most recently an international trade partner at Crowell & Moring and Kutner was most recently counsel at Sidley Austin .

— Michele Jawando has been announced as the next president of Omidyar Network . She previously has been senior vice president.

Borman was previously principal deputy assistant secretary for strategic trade and technology security at the Bureau of Industry and Security, and Albanese was previously director of BIS’ Office of National Security Controls.

— Bill Hildebrand is now a partner at MAD Global Strategy . He was previously a managing director.

— Liz Walters will be CEO of Democratic political data firm TargetSmart , per Signal Cleveland ’s Andrew Tobias . She currently is chair of the Ohio Democratic Party , which she’ll resign next month.

— Usha Sahay is now managing director for executive communications at the Rockefeller Foundation . She most recently was a speechwriter at the State Department and is a DOE, DOD and POLITICO alum.

— Sarah Guggenheimer is joining Planned Parenthood Federation of America as federal advocacy director. She previously was communications director for Senate Majority PAC and is a Mark Kelly alum.

HIRED GUNS: Sig Sauer has added the gun lobby’s former top lobbyist to its lineup of outside firms. The German handgun maker and defense manufacturer retained Capitol 6 Advisors , the firm started by Chris Cox after stepping down as the chief lobbyist at the National Rifle Association , back in February, according to a newly filed disclosure.

— Capitol 6 Advisors’ Phil Hoon and Stephanie Gadbois are working on the account as well on issues related to small arms manufacturing, gun regulations and foreign military sales.

— Despite spending more than two decades at the NRA, Sig Sauer is the first gun manufacturer Cox has registered to lobby for since starting his firm in 2019. Sig Sauer also retains Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld .

MORE NEW BUSINESS: The National Association of Broadcasters has brought one of its former lobbyists back into the fold after a stint in the public sector. Grisella Martinez worked for the trade group for four years before moving on to become then-Rep. Ruben Gallego ’s (D-Ariz.) chief of staff.

— Martinez then served as former Vice President Kamala Harris ’ legislative affairs director before transitioning over to Harris’ presidential campaign last year. Martinez launched her own lobbying firm, Axis Mundi , in January. NAB is her first lobbying client thus far.

— Anthropic , the company behind the artificial intelligence chatbot Claude , also added to its outside lobbying roster. The AI company retained Continental Strategy ’s Paul Calkins and Alberto Martinez , a former chief of staff to now-Secretary of State Marco Rubio , to lobby on AI development and national security, according to a disclosure filing. Anthropic also retains Aquia Group and Tower 19 .

Happy Wednesday and welcome to PI . Happy conclave to all who celebrate . Send K Street and, if you got ‘em, Vatican tips: You can add me on Signal , email me at [email protected] , and be sure to follow me on X : @caitlinoprysko .

ON THE AIRWAVES: The maritime industry is pouring six figures into a new ad blitz in defense of the Jones Act, the century-old law that bans foreign-flagged, foreign-built and foreign-crewed ships from carrying goods between U.S. ports.

— The 30-second spot from the American Maritime Partnership , American Waterways Operators and the Transportation Institute casts the Jones Act as core to President Donald Trump ’s “America First” agenda, arguing that “a secure America starts on our waters.”

— “America’s maritime remains core to our security and self-reliance,” the spot continues. It will run on digital and cable channels in D.C., including on Fox News, CNBC and CNN, and comes as members of AWO — which represents the tugboat, towboat and barge industry — will bring their defense of the Jones Act to the Hill next week for an industry “barge-in.”

— Trump has vowed to strengthen the domestic shipbuilding and maritime industry, which the Jones Act is aimed at reinforcing, but Project 2025, the conservative policy blueprint spearheaded by the Heritage Foundation , called for a potential repeal of the law.

MEME’S THE WORD: “Wall Street investors scoffed at it. Democrats have railed against it. But cryptocurrency traders can’t get enough” of Trump’s memecoin POLITICO ’s Declan Harty writes. “In the two weeks since plans for an exclusive dinner with the $TRUMP memecoin’s namesake were unveiled, a rush of interest has boosted the once-flagging collectible crypto token and reignited a firestorm on Capitol Hill .”

RELATED READ: “Top Trump Crypto Buyers Vying for Dinner Seats Are Likely Foreign, Data Shows,” by Bloomberg ’s Leonardo Nicoletti , Anthony Cormier and David Kocieniewski .

THE COST OF FREEDOM: Trump has enthusiastically wielded his clemency power so far in his second administration, with a soft spot in particular “for displays of loyalty and gripes about prosecutorial overreach.” A cottage industry of well-connected — and handsomely-paid — lawyers is cashing in on the “supercharged” pardon economy amid a “breakdown in the traditional vetting process for deciding who gets relief,”, Bloomberg ’s Ava Benny-Morrison and Bill Allison report.

— “These defendants with means are spending big for a chance to clear their names, at least in official records if not in public perception. Interviews with about two dozen lawyers and pardon hopefuls, many of whom asked not to be identified discussing plans that weren’t public, have pulled back the curtain on the clemency process under Trump.”

— “Some outlined plans to spend at least tens of thousands of dollars on attorneys, lobbyists and consultants, while others say the costs will reach well north of $1 million to put cases together and get them in front of the White House.”

NOTHING’S SET IN STONE: The Portland Cement Association , the cement industry’s main trade group, has rebranded as the American Cement Association . “Portland cement” refers to the most common kind of cement and was so named in 1824 because inventor Joseph Aspdin thought it looked like limestone from the Isle of Portland in England.

— President and CEO Mike Ireland said the name change reflects that U.S. manufacturers have increased their production of lower-emission forms of cement, such as portland-limestone cement, which has about a 10 percent lower carbon footprint.

PHARMING IT OUT: “President Donald Trump plans to revive an effort to dramatically slash drug costs by tying the amount the government pays for some medicines to lower prices abroad,” three people familiar with the matter told POLITICO ’s Jake Traylor and Adam Cancryn .

— “Trump early next week is expected to sign an executive order directing aides to pursue the initiative, called ‘most favored nation,’ for a selection of drugs within the Medicare program. The idea would use the administration’s authorities to force prices down,” though people involved in the plan cautioned it had not yet been finalized and that Trump had yet to personally approve it.

— The move would set up a major clash between Trump and the drug industry, which has told members of Congress that the policy could cost drug companies up to $1 trillion over a decade, Bloomberg ’s Rachel Cohrs Zhang reports.

— Trump’s plan has “drawn the industry off the sidelines, with several senior executives preparing to barnstorm Capitol Hill this week, according to nearly a dozen industry lobbyists and consultants who were not authorized to speak publicly about their efforts. … The brand-drug lobby PhRMA held an emergency call with its board members on Sunday to discuss its opposition strategy, some of the lobbyists said.”

FLYING IN: Intuit is flying in members of its Small Business Council in honor of National Small Business Week (hence all of the other small business-centric fly-ins we’ve seen this week). Small business owners will meet with Reps. Sam Liccardo (D-Calif.) and Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.) as well as staff for members of the Senate Banking Committee to discuss payment modernization efforts.

— CEOs with the American Council of Life Insurers were on the Hill today to meet with congressional offices finalizing the reconciliation bill. The nearly two dozen attendees sought to dissuade lawmakers from eliminating the state and local tax deduction for businesses, arguing that doing so could harm life insurers’ trillions of dollars in investments in the U.S. economy.

— More than 100 stakeholders from the dietary supplement industry are heading to the Hill for the Natural Products Association ’s annual fly-in. Industry representatives will highlight priorities they say are in line with HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. ’s Make America Healthy Again movement, such as expanding HSA and FSA reimbursement eligibility for dietary supplements, reshoring the supplement supply chain and preserving FDA’s regulation of supplements.

— The National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies ’ state-by-state fly-in is also underway, with members Arkansas, Maine, Michigan, North Carolina and Texas in town this week to meet with lawmakers on both sides of the Capitol. Delegations from Illinois, Iowa, New Jersey and Ohio were on the Hill last week to lobby on issues related to forest management and wildfire mitigation, the federal government’s ability to subpoena information from insurers and third-party litigation funding.

— Members of the Plant Based Products Council — which represents producers of everything from plant-based packaging to biofuels — are in town as well, as are title professionals represented by the American Land Title Association , the Orthodox Union Advocacy Center and cell tower workers with NATE: The Communications Infrastructure Contractors Association .

— Meanwhile, advocates with the National Brain Tumor Society will wrap up their fly-in today, which included more than 240 meetings on the books to make the case for increased research funding and a formal recognition of Brain Tumor Awareness Month and Glioblastoma Awareness Day.

— ACT | The App Association is also wrapping up a three-day fly-in focused on connecting small and medium-sized tech companies with lawmakers to discuss policy related to AI, data privacy, patent pricing, taxes, FSA and HSA eligibility for certain wearables devices and more. More than 45 member companies had more than 100 meetings scheduled throughout the week, including with lawmakers from the House Judiciary and Ways and Means committees.

— And at a meet and greet for freshman lawmakers hosted by the National Association of Manufacturers and GOP freshman class president Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas), per a tipster: Reps.
